a272.speaker: Ministry of Agriculture of Somalia
a272.name: Ministry of Agriculture of Somalia
a272.speech: Somalia has this week exported 17 tons of bananas to Saudi Arabia and Turkey, the Ministry of Agriculture has said.

a272.speaker: Yusuf Nur Eid, Somali Minister of Agriculture
a272.name: Yusuf Nur Eid
a272.title: Somali Minister of Agriculture
a272.speech: Speaking in Mogadishu, said the ship carrying the consignment left the port of Mogadishu for the international market this week.

a272.speaker: Yusuf Nur Eid, Somali Minister of Agriculture
a272.name: Yusuf Nur Eid
a272.title: Somali Minister of Agriculture
a272.speech: said the government was finalizing policies and regulatory frameworks to revive the banana sector in the country ; "We are finalizing the policies necessary to revive the Banana Marketing Agency to boost our exports to the international market. The agency will be unveiled soon."

a558.speaker: Prince Kermue Moye, Senator and Chairman of the Bong County Legislative Caucus (Liberia)
a558.name: Prince Kermue Moye
a558.title: Senator and Chairman of the Bong County Legislative Caucus (Liberia)
a558.speech: Speaking during the launch of the initiative, pointed out that the initiative was intended to buttress the government's efforts in providing healthcare delivery to its citizens; said the cancellation of United States Agency for International Development's (USAID) support to critical sectors in Liberia by the administration of President Donald Trump has affected most of the country's health programs; noted that as a result Liberia now needs partners like Doctors Without Borders who would fill in the gap to guarantee the health and wellbeing of its citizens, adding that "this partnership is one of such that all of us feel proud and we are so appreciative."

a558.speaker: Prince Kermue Moye, Senator and Chairman of the Bong County Legislative Caucus (Liberia)
a558.name: Prince Kermue Moye
a558.title: Senator and Chairman of the Bong County Legislative Caucus (Liberia)
a558.speech: Emphasized that citizens from other counties residing in Bong will also benefit from the treatment. "This is not your first time. We want to say thank you for coming and we cherish this partnership. This should not be the end. The team from the Executive and Legislature will continue to put small resources together to enhance your work and impact our people positively." ; "What we have been charged as a people is to always seek assistance for the betterment of our citizens. That will be one of our expectations. This is not going to be the end because we have explored opportunities for our citizens in different fields and this is just coming at the time it is much needed. We hope that those that have been screened and ready to go through the operations and medical care will be successful." ; "Once they are healthy, they will return to their different communities and provide services to the needy in those communities." He vowed to continue to work to positively impact the lives of his constituents and encouraged sons and daughters hailing from Bong to put aside their differences and rally around one another.

a558.speaker: Dr. Catherine Thomas Cooper, Chief Medical Officer of Liberia
a558.name: Dr. Catherine Thomas Cooper
a558.title: Chief Medical Officer of Liberia
a558.speech: Recounted the partnership between the Liberian government and Doctors Without Borders; observed that the return of the group to Liberia would not only benefit those seeking medical and surgical operations, but also health workers, including Liberian doctors and nurses; said skills would be transferred from the visiting Spanish doctors onto their Liberian counterparts; stressed that many of the patients across the country are financially constrained to seek adequate healthcare and as such the free medical and surgical operations are a welcoming venture. "We want to express our sincere gratitude for selecting Liberia as a country where you can provide expert services to our people. We are so grateful and we know that you have been where before and we treasure this partnership. We know that our health workers will benefit from your experience." ; maintained that the provision of proper care is expensive and that many of those in leeward areas are most often challenged, stating that the mission of the Spanish doctors "will really provide support to those patients who cannot afford and otherwise."

a558.speaker: Martha Morris, Deputy Minister for Administration at the Ministry of Health (Liberia)
a558.name: Martha Morris
a558.title: Deputy Minister for Administration at the Ministry of Health (Liberia)
a558.speech: "I'm so happy today that you (Spanish doctors) have accepted to be in Liberia and left your comfort zone to come and serve our people and you are starting from Bong County. Today it is Bong, your next trip will be to another county until you tour the whole Liberia."

a558.speaker: Antonio Satorra, Team Leader and General Surgeon
a558.name: Antonio Satorra
a558.title: Team Leader and General Surgeon
a558.speech: Assured that the team will do "a big job" that would save lives in Liberia; disclosed that the team will carry out surgical operations on more than 100 patients in Bong; expressed gratitude for the reception and level of support his team continues to receive from Senator Moye and other eminent citizens of the county, noting that "we will start as soon as possible and we will do as much as we can."

a564.speaker: Helen Boyle, Vice-President and Director of Programme Strategy of the International Development Division of EDC
a564.name: Helen Boyle
a564.title: Vice-President and Director of Programme Strategy of the International Development Division of EDC
a564.speech: Affirmed that the EDC and IESC consortium is happy to note that the government of Djibouti and the USAID Mission in Djibouti consider youth employment to be one of the country's economic and social development priorities. "We believe in creating lifelong employment opportunities for young men and women" ; said the interest of the government of Djibouti was demonstrated through the commitment of the representatives of MENFOP, ANEFIP and the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce to the participatory co-creation process, which made it possible to grasp the realities of the market ecosystem, identify the specific needs of vulnerable young people and produce the implementation action plan for the first year of the activity.

a564.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a564.name: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud
a564.title: Minister of National Education and Vocational Training of Djibouti
a564.speech: Indicated that bringing together the assembled efforts is essential to the success of this project. "The combination of our experiences and expertise in the field of workforce development is a precious asset," he stressed; confirmed his full willingness to work in close collaboration throughout this project and said it would be necessary to create an environment favourable to vocational training and youth employment.

a564.speaker: Omar Abdi Said, Minister of Labour in charge of Formalisation and Social Protection of Djibouti
a564.name: Omar Abdi Said
a564.title: Minister of Labour in charge of Formalisation and Social Protection of Djibouti
a564.speech: Recalled that Djiboutian youth, like all the youth of the world, face many challenges linked to developing their potential, to training adapted to requirements and access to the labour market, and to access to financing for those who take the initiative of self-entrepreneurship; testified that the Head of State, His Excellency Ismail Omar Guelleh, has made a commitment to provide a response to this constraint through government action; said this response is intended to be inclusive, concrete, resilient in the long term and above all efficient with regard to the efforts made by all the stakeholders.

a564.speaker: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh, President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a564.name: Youssouf Moussa Dawaleh
a564.title: President of the Djibouti Chamber of Commerce
a564.speech: Explained that he is confident in this project, which will make it possible to consolidate the gains and reach the new objectives set; affirmed that by focusing this time on support to the private sector, the project is in line with the missions of the chamber of commerce; said that through the institution's Approved Management Centre companies are supported in management and advice and will be able to benefit from capacity building in determining and formulating their human resources needs, and that this, complemented by the study carried out, will ultimately make it possible to have a realistic projection of companies' needs for qualified labour.

a564.speaker: Zahra Youssouf, director in charge of training within the USAID mission in Djibouti
a564.name: Zahra Youssouf
a564.title: director in charge of training within the USAID mission in Djibouti
a564.speech: Presented the summary of activities for the enrolment period from April to September 2023.

a564.speaker: Business leaders present at the ceremony
a564.name: Business leaders present at the ceremony
a564.speech: Gave testimonies, having committed to collaborating on youth employment with the institutional partners and the USAID activity.

a712.speaker: Rev. Brian Kamwendo, Presidential Adviser on Religious Affairs
a712.name: Rev. Brian Kamwendo
a712.title: Presidential Adviser on Religious Affairs
a712.speech: Standing by the claim that 5,300 clerics have benefitted from K8.3 billion in loans; speaking in an interview, he shrugged off the growing skepticism from Malawi's top religious institutions, saying the loans were deliberately targeted at "fraternal clerics" under a pilot phase of the Faith Leaders Empowerment Scheme, not through official church channels. "We started with the fraternal because this was just a pilot phase with an expectation that we will later engage the mother bodies. So, it is not strange that they don't know who have benefitted," Kamwendo explained.

a712.speaker: Whyghtone Mweta, NEEF credit manager
a712.name: Whyghtone Mweta
a712.title: NEEF credit manager
a712.speech: Clarified that the clerics accessed the funds after forming groups, and were engaged in various businesses like grocery shops, farming, and mobile money services. "They are part of the broader ecosystem of Malawian entrepreneurs. We treat them as any eligible Malawian who can benefit from Neef loans," said Mweta.

a712.speaker: National Economic Empowerment Fund (NEEF)
a712.name: National Economic Empowerment Fund (NEEF)
a712.speech: Is standing by the claim that 5,300 clerics have benefitted from K8.3 billion in loans; NEEF refuted a separate report alleging that K5.8 billion was disbursed to just 11 pastors under a purported presidential initiative; the fund said earlier this year it aimed to disburse K150 billion to over 400,000 farmers and entrepreneurs by March 2025.

a712.speaker: Malawi Conference of Catholic Bishops (MCCB), Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) and Muslim Association of Malawi (MAM)
a712.name: Malawi Conference of Catholic Bishops (MCCB)
a712.title: Malawi Council of Churches (MCC) and Muslim Association of Malawi (MAM)
a712.speech: Have all publicly distanced themselves from Kamwendo's announcement made during the July 5 national worship service marking Malawi's 61st independence anniversary.

a712.speaker: Fr. Valeriano Mtseka, MCCB general secretary
a712.name: Fr. Valeriano Mtseka
a712.title: MCCB general secretary
a712.speech: Said he was unaware of any Catholic cleric - bishop or priest - who had benefitted from the loans.

a712.speaker: Rev. Billy Gama, MCC board chairperson
a712.name: Rev. Billy Gama
a712.title: MCC board chairperson
a712.speech: "Actually, I was right there at the prayers and I was shocked when I heard that statement. To the best of my knowledge, no one [from MCC] has benefitted. It might have been a political statement," Gama said.

a712.speaker: Sheikh Dinala Chabulika, MAM spokesperson
a712.name: Sheikh Dinala Chabulika
a712.title: MAM spokesperson
a712.speech: Said his association moved quickly to verify Kamwendo's claims - only to find "zero" beneficiaries among its members. "Write [the story] and tell them [government] that we [MAM] haven't found anyone [who received Neef loans]," said Chabulika.

a770.speaker: Harrison Bhasikoro, Deputy director in the Department of Agriculture Engineering, Mechanisation and Farm Infrastructure Development, Zimbabwe
a770.name: Harrison Bhasikoro
a770.title: Deputy director in the Department of Agriculture Engineering, Mechanisation and Farm Infrastructure Development, Zimbabwe
a770.speech: Said in an interview with New Ziana on the harvesting preparedness for the summer cropping season that the country is expecting a bumper harvest and the government wants to ensure a seamless harvesting process for farmers across the country. “Obviously the country is expecting a bumper harvest, so in as far as taking out the crop from the fields, that is harvesting of the crop, I think also as a country we are prepared to do that, especially when we are looking at combine harvesting services,” he said, adding that currently the country has 313 combine harvesters ; said with each combine able to harvest at least 10 hectares per day, their capacity to harvest the 2024/25 summer crop will be around 4 000 hectares per day: “So if we consider a 150-day harvesting, then our minimum capacity will be close to 700 000 hectares. So as a country we are prepared in as far as combine harvester services is concerned. It’s not like all farmers will request combine harvester services, but also some farmers will do shelling and thrashing, so from the study that we carried out, as a country we are also prepared in as far as thrashing and shelling services are concerned,” he said ; said the country has enough equipment both from the government and private players to provide thrashing and shelling services, and encouraged farmers who have not arranged for harvesting services to approach their offices either at provincial or district level and register ; said the government is also working closely with Agriculture Finance Leasing Company as well as the Agricultural and Rural Development Authority (ARDA) and other private entities to assist during the harvesting period: “So in a nutshell we are saying we are, as a country, prepared to harvest all the crop on time so that also for those who want to switch from summer to winter wheat, also we are putting arrangements on the ground so that we can actually remove the summer crop so that they can quickly switch to winter cropping,” he said ; said the government is working to achieve the national requirement for combine harvesters of 600 by the end of next year ; said the Zimbabwe government is in the process of procuring 80 combine harvesters from Belarus, bringing the total number of the machines to around 400 against a national demand of 600.

a864.speaker: Stanley Dlamini, Chief Executive Officer of the Eswatini National Council of Arts and Culture (ENCAC)
a864.name: Stanley Dlamini
a864.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Eswatini National Council of Arts and Culture (ENCAC)
a864.speech: Shared how the event showcased a vibrant array of talent, with Eswatini's Young Zesh and Tru Classic delivering electrifying performances that earned a standing ovation from a discerning audience ; Noted that the stage was alive with energy from a diverse line-up of performers, including Mthokozisi Ndaba, Yamke, Don Dada, Kingsmen, and the closing act, Aubrey Qwabe, adding that each artist contributed to a memorable evening, celebrating the richness of regional artistic talent.

a864.speaker: Stanley Dlamini, Chief Executive Officer of the Eswatini National Council of Arts and Culture (ENCAC)
a864.name: Stanley Dlamini
a864.title: Chief Executive Officer of the Eswatini National Council of Arts and Culture (ENCAC)
a864.speech: Expressed appreciation for the warm reception accorded to the Eswatini artists and delegation in Sandton, specifically acknowledging the presence and instrumental role of Eswatini National Arts and Culture Awards (NACA) Chairperson Sipho Makhabane; he reiterated the need for continued collaboration and extended an invitation to South African media to further promote Eswatini talent, highlighting the interconnectedness of the global village.

a864.speaker: Stanley Khoza, AIRCO Deputy Chairperson
a864.name: Stanley Khoza
a864.title: AIRCO Deputy Chairperson
a864.speech: Speaking at the event, extended heartfelt gratitude to the ENCAC CEO for facilitating this pivotal collaboration: "This is just the beginning of many more collaborations between our two nations," emphasising the strategic importance of cross-border artistic exchange.

a864.speaker: Stanley Khoza, AIRCO Deputy Chairperson
a864.name: Stanley Khoza
a864.title: AIRCO Deputy Chairperson
a864.speech: Formally introduced Young Zesh and South African artist Yamke, confirming that they had entered the studio on Monday to record a collaborative track with a top-tier technical team; according to Khoza, Show Them Flames will oversee the post-production of the highly-anticipated song, with plans to visit Eswatini for its official launch.

a897.speaker: Vendors operating at the Opuwo Information and Cultural Centre
a897.name: Vendors operating at the Opuwo Information and Cultural Centre
a897.speech: Have appealed to authorities to improve the centre’s infrastructure; complained that the current sorry state of the centre was chasing away their clients; are now calling on the stakeholders to help improve the state of the centre.

a897.speaker: Gebhardt Makono, Opuwo Town Council support officer
a897.name: Gebhardt Makono
a897.title: Opuwo Town Council support officer
a897.speech: Said the town council plans to revamp and improve the centre to attract clients; however, he was quick to point out that no budget has been allocated yet, as the council is still busy with assessment.

a979.speaker: Xi Jinping, Chinese President
a979.name: Xi Jinping
a979.title: Chinese President
a979.speech: Solemnly proposed the Global Development Initiative on 21 September 2021 during the general debate of the 76th session of the United Nations General Assembly, bringing China's wisdom and strength to solving global development problems.

a979.speaker: China (at the High-level Dialogue on Global Development, June 2022)
a979.name: China (at the High-level Dialogue on Global Development
a979.title: June 2022)
a979.speech: Announced pragmatic measures to implement the initiative, notably transforming the South-South Cooperation Assistance Fund into the Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund, increasing its contribution to the UN Peace and Development Trust Fund, creating a Global Development Promotion Centre and a Global Development Knowledge Network, and publishing a Global Development Report.

a979.speaker: Stephen Bainous Kargbo, representative of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) in China
a979.name: Stephen Bainous Kargbo
a979.title: representative of the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) in China
a979.speech: Said the Global Development Initiative has helped mobilise resources, establish cooperation mechanisms and advance practical cooperation, and that the major progress achieved in areas such as poverty reduction, food security and health has demonstrated China's determination and capacity to contribute to global well-being and common prosperity.

a979.speaker: Carlos Maria Correa, executive director of the South Centre
a979.name: Carlos Maria Correa
a979.title: executive director of the South Centre
a979.speech: Noted that the Global Development Initiative aligns with the priorities of developing countries, emphasising the sustainable development goals and providing stronger and more targeted support to these nations.

a979.speaker: Dennis Francis, President of the 78th session of the United Nations General Assembly
a979.name: Dennis Francis
a979.title: President of the 78th session of the United Nations General Assembly
a979.speech: Stressed that the objectives of the Global Development Initiative are consistent with the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and have great potential to benefit countries around the world; the vision championed by the Initiative embodies the spirit of true multilateralism and will build a fairer and more sustainable world for all.

a1063.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a1063.name: Antonio Guterres
a1063.title: UN Secretary-General
a1063.speech: Condemned the shooting near a humanitarian aid distribution centre in the south of the Gaza Strip, which left 27 dead, a situation his spokesperson described as inconceivable.

a1063.speaker: Stephane Dujarric, spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General
a1063.name: Stephane Dujarric
a1063.title: spokesperson for the UN Secretary-General
a1063.speech: "It is unacceptable that civilians risk and, at times, lose their lives simply while looking for food," he told journalists, reiterating the call for an independent investigation already demanded after similar incidents this week.

a1063.speaker: Israeli Army
a1063.name: Israeli Army
a1063.speech: Announced that it had opened an investigation after the Red Cross confirmed the death of 27 Palestinians following a shooting near a humanitarian aid distribution centre in the south of the Gaza Strip.

a1063.speaker: Effie Defrin, spokesperson for the Israeli Army
a1063.name: Effie Defrin
a1063.title: spokesperson for the Israeli Army
a1063.speech: Said that on the previous morning Israeli soldiers "fired warning shots (...) at suspects who were approaching in a manner that put their safety at risk" ; "The incident is under investigation and we will fully clarify" what happened, he added, indicating that the Army "was not blocking the access of Gaza residents" to the humanitarian aid distribution points ; "On the contrary, we are allowing it. It is Hamas that is preventing that access."

a1063.speaker: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) (statement)
a1063.name: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) (statement)
a1063.speech: Confirmed the death of 27 people in the incidents near the humanitarian aid distribution centre: "Early this morning, the Red Cross's 60-bed field hospital in Rafah (south) received a massive influx of 184 patients. Nineteen of them were declared dead on arrival, and another eight succumbed to their injuries shortly afterwards. The majority of the patients had been shot."

a1063.speaker: Relief organisations in the Palestinian territory
a1063.name: Relief organisations in the Palestinian territory
a1063.speech: Had previously reported the death of 27 people in the incidents near the aid distribution centre.

a1063.speaker: Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF)
a1063.name: Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF)
a1063.speech: According to the organisation, the system of distribution points inside Israeli military zones aims to avoid Hamas.

a1063.speaker: United Nations
a1063.name: United Nations
a1063.speech: Rejected the new system, claiming that it does not respond to the growing hunger crisis in the territory and allows Israel to use humanitarian aid as a weapon.

a1063.speaker: Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF) (statement)
a1063.name: Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF) (statement)
a1063.speech: Announced in a statement that the Reverend Johnnie Moore, appointed commissioner for International Religious Freedom by the President of the United States, Donald Trump, will be its new director-general.

a1116.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a1116.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a1116.speech: Reported that between 25 and 31 May 2025, some 300 migrants were intercepted in the central Mediterranean and then returned to the Libyan coast, and that the operations were carried out off several Libyan coastal cities – Zuwara, Sabratha, Azzawiya, Tripoli and Al-Khums.

a1116.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a1116.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a1116.speech: Since the start of the year, the IOM counts 9,585 migrants returned to Libya, including 8,147 men, 960 women and 333 children, of whom 145 were unaccompanied minors or people requiring special assistance; as of 31 May 2025 at least 233 migrants had lost their lives at sea, while 225 others are reported missing. In 2024, 21,762 migrants had been intercepted, with a toll of 665 dead and 1,034 missing; the previous year there were 962 deaths and 1,536 disappearances at sea.

a1116.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a1116.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a1116.speech: Reiterates that Libya cannot be considered a safe port for the disembarkation of migrants. The organisation states that it is not involved in the interception operations, but provides humanitarian assistance on arrival, while calling for sustainable alternatives that respect fundamental rights.

a1248.speaker: John Roberts, US Supreme Court Chief Justice (ruling)
a1248.name: John Roberts
a1248.title: US Supreme Court Chief Justice (ruling)
a1248.speech: The top judge in the United States has given temporary backing to the Trump administration’s freeze on foreign aid payments; his intervention came as the administration faced a midnight deadline (05:00 GMT on Thursday) to pay contractors.

a1248.speaker: Trump administration officials
a1248.name: Trump administration officials
a1248.speech: Had argued that they could not process the payments within the timeframe set by a lower court judge ; as the deadline approached, the Trump administration went to the Supreme Court, arguing it was impossible to process claims in an orderly fashion in such a short period of time.

a1248.speaker: Amir Ali, US District Judge (court order)
a1248.name: Amir Ali
a1248.title: US District Judge (court order)
a1248.speech: Had ordered the US State Department and USAID to pay about $2bn-worth of bills (£1.6bn) to contractors by midnight on Wednesday.

a1248.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire Trump adviser
a1248.name: Elon Musk
a1248.title: billionaire Trump adviser
a1248.speech: Asked millions of bureaucrats over the weekend to list their accomplishments from the past week – sparking fury amongst the workforce and disagreement with officials leading the departments.

a1309.speaker: ZimTrade
a1309.name: ZimTrade
a1309.speech: According to ZimTrade, the market survey of Nigeria, whose full results will be presented to local companies, revealed huge opportunities for Zimbabwean products across sectors, including services.

a1365.speaker: Tanzania's Development Vision (TDV) 2050 (policy document)
a1365.name: Tanzania's Development Vision (TDV) 2050 (policy document)
a1365.speech: "acknowledges key issues including persistent poverty, the dominance of the informal economy, and the failure to process raw materials like cashews as some of the main bottlenecks for economic transformation in the country" ; "sets the ambitious target of turning Tanzania into a trillion-dollar economy from the current baseline of US$86 billion driven primarily by the private sector and Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs), with the government transitioning to an enabler of business" ; its first pillar "targets a strong, inclusive and competitive economy built on macroeconomic stability and predictability, fiscal sustainability, innovative and diversified financing"; its second pillar "aims to enhance human capital and create an inclusive, healthy society through education, health, social protection, housing, workforce development, and social cohesion"; its third pillar "acknowledges Tanzania's susceptibility to climate change and delineates ambitious environmental objectives across five domains: biodiversity, wetlands and water resources, environmental pollution, land management, and climate change resilience."

a1365.speaker: Tanzania's Development Vision (TDV) 2050 (policy document)
a1365.name: Tanzania's Development Vision (TDV) 2050 (policy document)
a1365.speech: Recognises a declining freedom of expression in Tanzania but falls short of outlining the key measures to reinstate and guarantee such freedom, noting that: "Freedom of expression remains constrained and has yet to meet societal expectations. The media space is limited, and professional and structural issues hinder open discourse." "Although the government has undertaken various efforts, corruption remains a persistent barrier hindering the realisation of social justice and inclusive development." It also acknowledges how communities are making significant investment in building social safety nets.

a1365.speaker: World Justice Project (ranking/report)
a1365.name: World Justice Project (ranking/report)
a1365.speech: Cited as the source for Tanzania "Ranking 96th out of 142 countries globally and 11th out of 34 countries in Sub-Saharan Africa", indicating that the country requires considerable investment in key institutions of accountability.

a1365.speaker: A 2014 study
a1365.name: A 2014 study
a1365.speech: "identified the lack of fairness, competence and neutrality of governance players as contributing to citizens not trusting in public parastatals in Tanzania, which could significantly hamper attempts to build a viable social protection economy."

a1681.speaker: John Bernon, director of USAID's health office
a1681.name: John Bernon
a1681.title: director of USAID's health office
a1681.speech: Notes that access to family planning services allows people to decide when to have children, how to space births and to choose the size of the family, and that the availability of contraceptive products plays an important role in these decisions and choices.

a1681.speaker: John Bernon, director of USAID's health office
a1681.name: John Bernon
a1681.title: director of USAID's health office
a1681.speech: Drawing on the 2021 contraception index report, points out that gaps of around 50% remain to be covered in terms of contraception and that it is urgent to continue efforts to close them in order to guarantee universal access to family planning services and thereby reduce maternal death rates. He says he is convinced of the need to favour a regional approach in the search for solutions to common challenges such as sustainable financing and the acquisition of contraceptives.

a1681.speaker: 2021 contraception index report (cited)
a1681.name: 2021 contraception index report (cited)
a1681.speech: Cited as showing that gaps of around 50% remain to be covered in terms of contraception.

a1681.speaker: Rodrigue Kohoun, representing the Minister of Health of Benin
a1681.name: Rodrigue Kohoun
a1681.title: representing the Minister of Health of Benin
a1681.speech: Stresses that the availability of contraceptive products is also indispensable for achieving Sustainable Development Goal No. 3: "It is an essential subject of development for our sub-region that brings us together here in Cotonou. Benin is resolutely committed to this path of development," while urging participants, on behalf of President Patrice Talon, to find innovative and applicable solutions for a sustainable improvement in the financing of family planning.

a1762.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1762.name: Donald Trump
a1762.title: US President
a1762.speech: Said the reciprocal tariffs were "for countries that treat us badly". During Wednesday's announcement at the White House, the Republican president said that the US had been taken advantage of by "cheaters" and had been "pillaged" by foreigners. "Our taxpayers have been ripped off for more than 50 years, but it is not going to happen any more." ; "It's our declaration of economic independence," he added while holding up a chart showing a list of countries that charge higher tariffs on US goods, impose "non-tariff" barriers to US trade or have otherwise acted in ways US officials feel undermine American economic goals.

a1762.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1762.name: Donald Trump
a1762.title: US President
a1762.speech: Said South Africa was among the countries dubbed the "worst offenders" that now face higher US rates – payback for unfair trade policies – and said his country would implement a "discounted" 30% tariff on South Africa. "They have got some bad things going on in South Africa. You know, we are paying them billions of dollars, and we cut the funding because a lot of bad things are happening in South Africa."

a1762.speaker: White House (data/list)
a1762.name: White House (data/list)
a1762.speech: According to the White House, in 2024 while the US exported just $2.8m (£2.1m) worth of goods to Lesotho, it imported $237.3m from the southern African country. The White House released a list of roughly 100 countries and the tariff rates that the US would impose on what Trump dubbed "liberation day" for the American people.

a1762.speaker: South African presidency (statement)
a1762.name: South African presidency (statement)
a1762.speech: In a statement, condemned the new tariffs as "punitive", saying they could "serve as a barrier to trade and shared prosperity".

a1998.speaker: Daniel Ndoye, African Development Bank (AfDB) Representative in Benin
a1998.name: Daniel Ndoye
a1998.title: African Development Bank (AfDB) Representative in Benin
a1998.speech: Proposed that one of the major challenges to be met in order to respond to the needs of traditionally under-served populations is the establishment of sound financial systems, noting that only 21% of adults on the continent have an account in formal financial institutions; pointed out that the development of such financial systems in Africa is one of the important levers of the AfDB’s actions to achieve the objectives of its 2013-2022 ten-year strategy on inclusive growth, and that the Patimf project fits well with this policy.

a1998.speaker: Valère Houssou, President of the Board of Directors of Consortium Alafia
a1998.name: Valère Houssou
a1998.title: President of the Board of Directors of Consortium Alafia
a1998.speech: Said that transparency is not a gain but rather an objective to be approached daily by every actor, and warned that Patimf will not be limited only to promoting price transparency in microfinance: “It will address more fully all the other elements of financial transparency, beginning with the regulatory framework applicable to decentralised financial systems (Sfd), their internal control system, the production of reliable information for the authority and for partners, external auditing, social performance management, promotion, and client protection” ; he continued that Apsfd-Benin, the clients and the Business Development Service (Bds) Providers will also see their capacities strengthened so as to really play their part for greater transparency within microfinance institutions.

a1998.speaker: Valère Houssou, President of the Board of Directors of Consortium Alafia
a1998.name: Valère Houssou
a1998.title: President of the Board of Directors of Consortium Alafia
a1998.speech: Promised that all the required indicators would be achieved, and indicated that Consortium Alafia had successfully implemented, among others, the project for institutional strengthening of the microfinance sector financed by USAID, the private sector development support project (Padsp) financed by the World Bank, and the MasterCard Foundation’s Mission Africa project for the promotion of social performance management.

a1998.speaker: Jacques Dougnon, Chief of Staff of the Minister in charge of Microfinance (Benin)
a1998.name: Jacques Dougnon
a1998.title: Chief of Staff of the Minister in charge of Microfinance (Benin)
a1998.speech: Said that these achievements testify to Consortium Alafia’s constant presence alongside the decentralised financial systems (Sfd).

a1998.speaker: Alphonso Barnuevo, Ambassador of Spain to Benin
a1998.name: Alphonso Barnuevo
a1998.title: Ambassador of Spain to Benin
a1998.speech: Acknowledged the relevance and interest of Patimf and reaffirmed Spain’s readiness to support Consortium Alafia in the proper execution of the project.

a1998.speaker: Nicaise Tossou, National Director for Benin and Togo of OIKO Credit
a1998.name: Nicaise Tossou
a1998.title: National Director for Benin and Togo of OIKO Credit
a1998.speech: Acknowledged the relevance and interest of Patimf and reaffirmed Oiko Credit’s readiness to support Consortium Alafia in the proper execution of the project, which is beneficial for the populations.

a2141.speaker: Kabalano Rampa, international trade expert
a2141.name: Kabalano Rampa
a2141.title: international trade expert
a2141.speech: In a televised interview on Monday, stated that Botswana is unlikely to feel the immediate effects of the impending fuel crisis: "We will definitely not experience the effects immediately in regards to our fuel prices going up as there are delayed and buffer effects." ; "We will experience them at a later time. It gives us an opportunity to start acting and preparing now."

a2141.speaker: Kabalano Rampa, international trade expert
a2141.name: Kabalano Rampa
a2141.title: international trade expert
a2141.speech: Noted that the proposed joint oil refinery deal between Namibia and Botswana could prove critical in the long run but said that it will be some time and cost before it is in place; he added that Botswana has the capacity to switch to solar and wind energy as alternative sources of fuel, and recommended intra-African trade as a means to mitigating the economic effects of the war.

a2141.speaker: Iran (government threat)
a2141.name: Iran (government threat)
a2141.speech: In response to airstrikes by the United States early Sunday, has threatened to close the Strait of Hormuz through which 20 percent of the world's oil supply of 20 million barrels pass per day.

a2152.speaker: William Ruto, President of Kenya
a2152.name: William Ruto
a2152.title: President of Kenya
a2152.speech: "The situation in Sudan is disastrous: millions of people have been displaced and more than 2,000 people have lost their lives," Ruto said in a statement following the meeting; he added that the intensity and scale of the humanitarian crisis constitute a heartbreaking tragedy that calls for a courageous and inclusive peace dialogue ; according to Ruto, "this step will lead to the resumption of the final phase of the political process, paving the way for the formation of an inclusive transitional process that will lay the foundations for a lasting peace and a stable and prosperous Sudan."

a2152.speaker: IGAD Quartet (press release)
a2152.name: IGAD Quartet (press release)
a2152.speech: Called on the parties to the conflict in Sudan to declare and observe an unconditional ceasefire, and to establish a humanitarian zone with a radius of 30 kilometres in Khartoum in order to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian aid.

a2152.speaker: Local health authorities (Sudan)
a2152.name: Local health authorities (Sudan)
a2152.speech: According to local health authorities, the conflict between the army and the paramilitaries of the Rapid Support Forces since April has killed nearly 3,000 people and wounded thousands among the civilian population.

a2172.speaker: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report (prepared by 25 Russian policy experts, headed by Sergei A. Karaganov, under a programme sponsored by the Russian Foreign Ministry)
a2172.name: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report (prepared by 25 Russian policy experts
a2172.title: headed by Sergei A. Karaganov, under a programme sponsored by the Russian Foreign Ministry)
a2172.speech: The report identifies two key factors necessary for determining the long-term importance of the continent: (i) human capital and (ii) natural resources; it offers new directions, some development prospects and recommendations for improving policy methods and approaches with Africa.

a2172.speaker: Some situation analysis participants who contributed to the policy report
a2172.name: Some situation analysis participants who contributed to the policy report
a2172.speech: spoke very critically of Russia's current policy towards Africa. They even claimed that there was no consistent policy and/or consistency in the policy implementation at all.

a2172.speaker: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report
a2172.name: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report
a2172.speech: "The situation analysis participants agreed that the lack of project due diligence and proper verification of contracting partners is one of the key challenges for Russian business in Africa. Many projects announced at the top and high political levels have not been implemented. The reason is usually that the projects were not properly prepared before official approval. As a result, budget funding is often spent on raw and unprepared initiatives."

a2172.speaker: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report
a2172.name: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report
a2172.speech: recommends that Russia compile its various ideas for cooperation with Africa into a single comprehensive and publicly available strategy, adopt an open doctrinal document on cooperation with Africa, present such a strategy at the second Russia-Africa summit and adopt an accompanying Action Plan.

a2172.speaker: All situation analysis participants
a2172.name: All situation analysis participants
a2172.speech: agreed that, unlike most competitors, Russia can afford to promote a more honest, open, direct and understandable agenda for Africa: sovereignty, continental integration, infrastructure development, human development (education and medicine), security (including the fight against hunger and epidemics), normal universal human values, the idea that people should live with dignity and feel protected.

a2172.speaker: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report
a2172.name: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report
a2172.speech: proposes that dialogues should be enhanced between civil societies, including expert and academic organizations, and that the humanitarian track can become one of the ways to deepen relations further.

a2172.speaker: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report
a2172.name: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report
a2172.speech: On foreign players in Africa, the report points to China as number one active player; India's influence continues to grow, as does the involvement of Turkey, the UAE, and Qatar. The influence and involvement of the United States, Japan, South Korea, and Brazil in the coming years are likely to remain at the level of the past decade and will decline compared to China's influence.

a2172.speaker: The authors of the report
a2172.name: The authors of the report
a2172.speech: Canada, Italy, and the UK, according to the authors, can at best maintain their influence at the same level, but it, too, will decrease compared to that of the new centers of power; of all the G7 countries, only Germany still has some potential to increase its influence and presence in Africa.

a2172.speaker: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report
a2172.name: The Russia-Africa Situation Analytical Report
a2172.speech: proposes discussions on possible mechanisms and formats of bilateral and multilateral alliances with interested parties whose interests in Africa may coincide with the Russian ones, for example India, and suggests exploring engagement with South Korea, Vietnam, Cuba, Serbia and several others.

a2172.speaker: The situation analysis participants
a2172.name: The situation analysis participants
a2172.speech: agreed that Russia's policy in Africa should be a derivative of Russia's overall foreign policy goals and objectives, the three key areas being: ensuring national security; ensuring social and economic development of Russia; and strengthening the position of the Russian Federation as one of the influential centers in the modern world.

a2199.speaker: Tullow Ghana Limited (letter dated May 29, 2025 to the Minister for Energy and Green Transition)
a2199.name: Tullow Ghana Limited (letter dated May 29
a2199.title: 2025 to the Minister for Energy and Green Transition)
a2199.speech: Officially withdrew its 2023 draft Amended Plan of Development (TAPOD) for the Tweneboa, Enyenra, and Ntomme (TEN) oil field and related Combined Gas Sales Agreement (CGSA), citing shifting market conditions, investment uncertainties, inflationary pressures, revised estimates of gas volumes, and the need for a revised long-term strategy; the letter explained that negotiations on the CGSA had already been paused in December 2023, and that proposals from the Ghana Negotiation Committee (GNC) on an acceptable Level 2 payment security mechanism, a critical component for further investment in the TEN gas infrastructure, were awaiting.

a2199.speaker: Jean-Médard Madama, Managing Director of Tullow Ghana
a2199.name: Jean-Médard Madama
a2199.title: Managing Director of Tullow Ghana
a2199.speech: Said the decision follows ongoing technical and commercial reassessments: "We write following our communication during the deep dive session held with you in April 2025, that the TEN Partners are reviewing the long-term plan for TEN" ; "Since the TEN business case supporting the TAPOD was developed in 2022, the underlying investment basis has changed" ; "Key developments include market changes, inflationary pressures, new cost reduction opportunities on the TEN FPSO, and improved understanding of the TEN field" ; stressed that realising the revised volumes would require further investment "underpinned by an appropriate commercial framework, including an economic gas price and acceptable payment security."

a2199.speaker: Jean-Médard Madama, Managing Director of Tullow Ghana
a2199.name: Jean-Médard Madama
a2199.title: Managing Director of Tullow Ghana
a2199.speech: Reaffirmed Tullow's commitment to Ghana's energy sector and the TEN field's long-term viability: "We remain committed to the TEN re-development priorities, including extending TEN's economic life, maximising resource recovery and safeguarding the viability of gas supply to Ghana" ; "We deeply value our partnership with the Government of Ghana and remain committed to ensuring the TEN field operates to its full potential and contributes significantly to the nation's energy security" ; says it is "progressing various workstreams to maximise TEN value and production", including efforts to access in-field exploration (ILX) rights and engaging potential third-party interim gas offtakers.

a2199.speaker: Energynewsafrica.com
a2199.name: Energynewsafrica.com
a2199.speech: Reports that the withdrawal of the plan raises questions about the investment needed to develop the TEN field further and potential implications for gas prices in Ghana.

a2199.speaker: Industry experts
a2199.name: Industry experts
a2199.speech: Believe this development poses a significant threat to the realisation of the country's plan to construct a second gas processing plant (GPP2).

a2199.speaker: A source familiar with the gas industry (anonymous)
a2199.name: A source familiar with the gas industry (anonymous)
a2199.speech: Said that justifying GPP2 with only a firm export flow of 160 mmscfd from both Jubilee and TEN will be challenging.

a2199.speaker: Operational experts
a2199.name: Operational experts
a2199.speech: Believe there won't be much gas left for the proposed GPP2, with the existing gas processing plant operated by Ghana National Gas Company having a capacity of 150 mmscfd.

a2208.speaker: Transitional authorities of Niger (official statement/communiqué)
a2208.name: Transitional authorities of Niger (official statement/communiqué)
a2208.speech: Denounced on Friday in a statement the EU's granting of 1.3 million euros in humanitarian aid without their having been informed beforehand: "The EU ambassador in Niger has, unilaterally," redistributed this aid to NGOs, "in disregard of the principles of transparency and good collaboration with the competent Nigerien authorities"; the statement added that an "audit" of the management of the funds in question has been requested.

a2208.speaker: Spokesperson for the EU diplomatic service (European External Action Service)
a2208.name: Spokesperson for the EU diplomatic service (European External Action Service)
a2208.speech: Said the EU expresses its "deep disagreement" after what it denounces as a "calling into question" of the arrangements for managing the humanitarian aid it provided to the victims of the severe floods that struck the country. "As a result, the EU has decided to recall its ambassador from Niamey for consultations in Brussels," he added ; said the EU "wants to continue to support the population."

a2400.speaker: Fanta Sadibou Koné, director of the NGO and job creation forum
a2400.name: Fanta Sadibou Koné
a2400.title: director of the NGO and job creation forum
a2400.speech: Explained that this event is the ideal space to strengthen this partnership, to discover and better understand the role of each actor and to strengthen collaboration; she went on that this 1st edition will also allow the establishment of a centralised database listing the jobs created by NGOs, whether through humanitarian or development projects, and noted that during these two days of conferences and panel discussions there will be a new path in the recognition, sharing and strengthening of a lasting partnership. “NGOs do not merely provide humanitarian aid; they play an essential role in Mali’s economic development by creating jobs, training young people and supporting entrepreneurship.” ; She noted that NGOs play a crucial role in job creation in Mali, notably by supporting entrepreneurship, strengthening young people’s skills and facilitating access to the labour market, adding that NGOs recruit staff for their projects, thereby offering employment opportunities in various fields.

a2400.speaker: Fanta Sadibou Koné, director of the NGO and job creation forum
a2400.name: Fanta Sadibou Koné
a2400.title: director of the NGO and job creation forum
a2400.speech: Said that NGOs employ thousands of people such as technical staff, field agents, trainers, logisticians, human resources staff and specialists in various fields. “Despite their commitment, NGOs face many obstacles: insecurity, limited access to certain areas, communities’ mistrust, or the difficulties of long-term financing for employment projects,” she lamented. She stated that they suffer from the decline in and dependence on funding, the mismatch between training and the labour market, political and security instability, and weak coordination among actors.

a2400.speaker: Fanta Sadibou Koné, director of the NGO and job creation forum
a2400.name: Fanta Sadibou Koné
a2400.title: director of the NGO and job creation forum
a2400.speech: Specified that for the year 2024, more than 65 organisations have over 3,998 active employees, of whom 95% are nationals; 4,242 young people benefited from socio-professional integration training and 66,601 people were supported in income-generating activities. “3,242 teachers received training, 8,538 health workers were trained on health themes (SSRD, nutrition, WASH, etc.), 47,089 people were trained in agricultural techniques.” According to her, 11,590 people were trained in livestock techniques and 32,766 benefited from training sessions on environmental protection.

a2400.speaker: Adama Cissouma, Secretary General of the Ministry of Territorial Administration and Decentralisation
a2400.name: Adama Cissouma
a2400.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Territorial Administration and Decentralisation
a2400.speech: Commended the Ministry of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training and stressed that this forum represents a major opportunity to encourage innovation, bring initiatives together and catalyse energies in favour of a future where every Malian can live with dignity from their work.

a2400.speaker: Oumou Sall Seck, Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training
a2400.name: Oumou Sall Seck
a2400.title: Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training
a2400.speech: Stated that she has mandated the National Observatory of Employment and Training (ONEF) to conduct an in-depth study on the training and job-creation actions carried out by NGOs across the country, whose conclusions will enrich the discussions and guide strategic decisions ; maintained that the forum is intended to be a strategic space for consultation, recognition and synergy to strengthen convergences between NGO initiatives, public employment policies and the entrepreneurial dynamics of the private sector ; “This forum thus aims at better visibility of the training mechanisms and jobs created by NGOs, and at the consolidation and structuring of their contribution, through the establishment of a permanent framework of dialogue bringing together public institutions, NGOs, technical and financial partners, as well as economic operators.” ; stressed that the Job Cluster forum constitutes a major step forward in the shared ambition to build a united, prosperous and inclusive Mali, and specified that it forms part of an ambitious government vision in which employment becomes a foundation of national reconstruction.

a2402.speaker: Study published in the journal Nature Food (May 2025)
a2402.name: Study published in the journal Nature Food (May 2025)
a2402.speech: According to the study, which assessed 186 countries based on their ability to feed their populations across seven major food groups, Malawi has been ranked among the top 50 most food self-sufficient countries in the world, alongside seven other African nations; Malawi scored particularly high in the production of fruits (243%) and starchy staples (221%) but lags in dairy production, achieving only 17% of national requirements. Other African countries in the top 50 include Mali, Niger, Cameroon, Senegal, South Sudan, Tunisia and Morocco; Mali topped the African pack with self-sufficiency in fruits (107%) and starchy staples (236%), while South Sudan had a dairy score of 303%.

a2402.speaker: Study published in the journal Nature Food (May 2025)
a2402.name: Study published in the journal Nature Food (May 2025)
a2402.speech: The report also warns that food self-sufficiency does not automatically translate to food security, and that many African nations still face significant hurdles, including climate shocks (droughts, floods, erratic rainfall), inadequate storage infrastructure, limited access to irrigation and mechanized farming, and weak value chains and market access.

a2402.speaker: Agriculture experts in Malawi
a2402.name: Agriculture experts in Malawi
a2402.speech: Have welcomed the ranking, noting that it offers encouragement to policymakers to invest more strategically in the sector.

a2402.speaker: Dr. Thokozani Maluwa, agricultural economist based in Lilongwe
a2402.name: Dr. Thokozani Maluwa
a2402.title: agricultural economist based in Lilongwe
a2402.speech: “This shows that our small-scale farmers are doing something right. What we need now is investment in value addition, irrigation, and post-harvest technologies to bridge the gap in areas like dairy and protein.”

a2402.speaker: Experts (Malawi)
a2402.name: Experts (Malawi)
a2402.speech: Say the country must invest in expanding irrigation schemes to reduce reliance on rain-fed agriculture, scaling up livestock and dairy development, building resilient value chains for fruits and vegetables, and enhancing access to financing, inputs, and training for smallholder farmers.

a2402.speaker: Patricia Nkhoma, nutritionist
a2402.name: Patricia Nkhoma
a2402.title: nutritionist
a2402.speech: “This is not just about growing more food, but about growing the right food, in the right quantities, and ensuring it reaches the people who need it most.”

a2679.speaker: Chitungwiza Municipality (City Fathers)
a2679.name: Chitungwiza Municipality (City Fathers)
a2679.speech: Say the over US$2 billion owed by ratepayers is affecting the local authority's capacity to provide efficient services.

a2679.speaker: Japson Nemuseso, Acting Town Clerk of Chitungwiza Municipality
a2679.name: Japson Nemuseso
a2679.title: Acting Town Clerk of Chitungwiza Municipality
a2679.speech: In a notice on Thursday, said the door-to-door revenue collection will also enhance convenience for residents and other stakeholders: "Valued residents and other stakeholders are encouraged to take advantage of this convenience. Our teams will be moving around residential areas and business centres with point-of-sale (POS) machines, allowing you to pay bills from the comfort of your homes, offices, or businesses." ; "The teams comprise uniformed municipal police officers and cashiers. Cash payments are accepted. Please note that the teams will also be collecting vital statistics at each household or premise to update the council's database. The officials will request mobile numbers to enable the council to send bills electronically via text messages or emails. We encourage all stakeholders to take advantage of this exercise to clear their outstanding bills."

a2752.speaker: Christine Umutoni, UN Resident Coordinator in Liberia
a2752.name: Christine Umutoni
a2752.title: UN Resident Coordinator in Liberia
a2752.speech: Reaffirmed the UN Country Team's commitment to assisting Liberia in achieving the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development and emphasized the importance of continued support for Liberia's peacebuilding efforts, making specific reference to strengthening national institutions, enhancing human rights protection, and fostering social inclusion ; Stressed that the UN is aware of the challenges posed by the recent aid cut by the United States Government and its impact on implementing the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development.

a2752.speaker: Sara Beysolow-Nyanti, Liberian Foreign Minister
a2752.name: Sara Beysolow-Nyanti
a2752.title: Liberian Foreign Minister
a2752.speech: Recognized significant progress made by Liberia in its recovery and development journey, but noted that challenges remain, especially in areas such as unemployment, healthcare, and infrastructure; called for increased international support, particularly in capacity building, job creation, and sustainable economic development ; Highlighted the need for the UN to remain flexible and responsive to Liberia's evolving needs, particularly in the face of global challenges like health crises and economic downturns; called for a stronger UN presence in Liberia's rural areas, where much of the country's population resides, and advocated for a greater focus on inclusive development programs that would benefit marginalized and underserved communities.

a2752.speaker: Liberian Foreign Ministry (release)
a2752.name: Liberian Foreign Ministry (release)
a2752.speech: According to a Foreign Ministry release, the meeting, held quarterly, is part of Minister Nyanti's ongoing efforts to strategically engage with development partners in the country.

a2818.speaker: Sam Pee Yalley, Ghana's former High Commissioner to India
a2818.name: Sam Pee Yalley
a2818.title: Ghana's former High Commissioner to India
a2818.speech: He often credited his academic journey with equipping him for the challenges of governance and diplomacy, and he remained a staunch advocate for education and youth empowerment ; he publicly championed efforts to promote women into leadership roles and frequently used his platform to challenge societal norms and push for inclusive governance, believing that national development could only be achieved through equal participation by all.

a2827.speaker: Dambisa Moyo, author of the book Dead Aid
a2827.name: Dambisa Moyo
a2827.title: author of the book Dead Aid
a2827.speech: In her landmark book, Dead Aid, discusses why aid does not really work in most African countries that are dependent on the West for survival ; she views the aid that comes to these countries as harmful because it perpetuates corruption and dependency, rather than promoting sustainable development and economic growth ; as Moyo observes, more than 50 years of aid from the West has not significantly developed Africa.

a2827.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a2827.name: Donald Trump
a2827.title: US President
a2827.speech: Has echoed Moyo's sentiments and, among other things, has frozen aid provided through the US Agency for International Development (USAID), threatening to completely shut the agency down.

a2827.speaker: Government of Malawi
a2827.name: Government of Malawi
a2827.speech: Has said that it is looking for alternatives to USAID.

a2879.speaker: Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) (court filing)
a2879.name: Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) (court filing)
a2879.speech: The case, filed on June 12, 2025, at the High Court (Criminal Division) in Accra by the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP), implicates the four in a range of offenses, including corruption, abuse of office, conspiracy to steal, and attempted theft, among them the use of a forged letter, purportedly from the Office of the Vice President, to facilitate the fraud.

a2879.speaker: Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP)
a2879.name: Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP)
a2879.speech: According to the OSP, between April and July 2022, the four conspired to unlawfully acquire the rice containers, valued at over $200,000, despite having no ownership rights.

a2879.speaker: Court documents
a2879.name: Court documents
a2879.speech: Reveal that in November 2021, a local businessman entered into a contract with Lele Group of Companies in Thailand to import rice under the name Faithy Ventures. The full payment - $204,777 - was made to Suwamaphum Rice Co. Ltd.

a2879.speaker: Prosecutors
a2879.name: Prosecutors
a2879.speech: Allege that this is when the accused began manipulating systems to fraudulently take possession of the containers ; Seidu is alleged to have submitted falsified documents, including a forged letter bearing the name of the Office of the Vice President, to request the unlawful release of the rice ; Abban and Hyde are accused of recommending and facilitating the auctioning of the rice to Seidu, despite knowing he had no legal claim to it.

a2946.speaker: Andre Ndereyimana, advocacy, research and communication officer at ActionAid-Burundi
a2946.name: Andre Ndereyimana
a2946.title: advocacy, research and communication officer at ActionAid-Burundi
a2946.speech: "The mining sector influences the standard of living and the socio-economic and financial health of countries." ; Indicated that Burundi's subsoil is rich in gold, tantalum, tin, tungsten and rare earths, as well as industrial minerals including kaolin, phosphates and limestone. ; On behalf of ActionAid, insists on good governance and transparency in Burundi's mining sector in order to facilitate and increase state revenues from minerals, in particular at this time when financing through foreign aid is dwindling; recalls that the rational and responsible exploitation of mineral resources benefits citizens, essentially the population living near the deposit sites.

a2946.speaker: Study on "domestic resource mobilisation and natural resource governance in Burundi" (commissioned by ActionAid in collaboration with Christian Aid)
a2946.name: Study on "domestic resource mobilisation and natural resource governance in Burundi" (commissioned by ActionAid in collaboration with Christian Aid)
a2946.speech: According to this study, Burundi holds 6% of the world's nickel reserves.

a2946.speaker: Damien Mbonicuye and Jean Berchmans Ndikumana, researchers
a2946.name: Damien Mbonicuye and Jean Berchmans Ndikumana
a2946.title: researchers
a2946.speech: Said mining could contribute considerably to job creation and diversify Burundi's economy; nevertheless they deplore that this sector contributes only 1% of GDP and 3% of the country's export revenues.

a2946.speaker: ActionAid (NGO)
a2946.name: ActionAid (NGO)
a2946.speech: Undertakes to convey to decision-makers the recommendations arising from the discussions on this study.

a2995.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2995.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2995.speech: Said it has reached a staff-level agreement with Somalia on the third review under the Extended Credit Facility arrangement ; said in a statement issued on Friday evening that the deal would see the lender unlock 10 million U.S. dollars, which is subject to approval of the IMF Executive Board.

a2995.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2995.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2995.speech: Estimated a 4 percent growth in Somalia's real gross domestic product in 2024, driven by continued agricultural recovery, while inflation is expected to ease to 5.6 percent by the end of 2024, supported by lower global commodity prices.

a2995.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2995.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2995.speech: Said the country's economic outlook in 2025 is clouded by foreign aid cuts, irregular rainfalls and high uncertainty in the country ; "Real GDP growth in 2025 is expected to slow to 3 percent amid weaker private consumption and imports. Inflation is projected to decelerate to 4.9 percent by the end of 2025, though the pace is slower than previously anticipated," adding that downside risks dominate the near-term outlook.

a2995.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2995.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2995.speech: Said fiscal reforms continue to progress steadily while the Somali authorities recognize the importance of accelerating efforts to build stronger public finances.

a2995.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2995.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2995.speech: Warned that a more severe and sustained reduction in foreign aid would have long-term economic consequences, exacerbate food insecurity and poverty, deteriorate human development indicators, and jeopardize Somalia's progress in rebuilding institutional capacity.

a3238.speaker: Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's first President (speech at the founding of the Organization of African Unity, Addis Ababa, 1963)
a3238.name: Dr. Kwame Nkrumah
a3238.title: Ghana's first President (speech at the founding of the Organization of African Unity, Addis Ababa, 1963)
a3238.speech: Emphasized the urgency of African unity and the need for collective economic planning to effectively harness the continent's potential resources. He warned that without such unity and concerted effort, Africa would struggle to progress at the necessary pace, and its challenges could become chronic, making it too late for Pan-African unity to ensure stability and prosperity.

a3238.speaker: Africa Prosperity 2024 Presidential and Business Executive Dialogue Peduase Compact 2024 (joint declaration presented by Africa-America Institute President Kofi Appenteng)
a3238.name: Africa Prosperity 2024 Presidential and Business Executive Dialogue Peduase Compact 2024 (joint declaration presented by Africa-America Institute President Kofi Appenteng)
a3238.speech: Committed business leaders, elected officials and social impact leaders to advancing the African Continental Free Trade Area Agreement with the goal of empowering African nations in their pursuit of prosperity: "We emphasised that the primary goal of the Africa Prosperity Network is to shift the narrative in African countries from 'poverty reduction' to one that empowers nations in their pursuit of prosperity." ; "We believe that it is both necessary and urgent for Africa's private sector, from large-scale to small and medium-scale enterprises (SMEs), to own and drive the continent's single market agenda." ; committed the business community to interoperable payment systems, value-added manufacturing, digitalisation and agri-technology; governments to public-private infrastructure partnerships, trade facilitation, visa-free arrangements among all African countries, investment in agriculture and value addition of natural resources, and to advocating the creation of a reparation infrastructural fund; the AfCFTA Secretariat to supporting non-ratifying member States; and development partners including the UN, UNDP, UNECA, WFP, AfDB, Afreximbank, BADEA, BOAD and EBID to coordinated support and technical assistance ; "We commit to meet annually, under the Africa Prosperity Dialogues, to take stock of the progress of Africa's Prosperity Agenda" ; "We thank H.E. Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo and the government of the Republic of Ghana for spearheading the Africa Prosperity Dialogues."

a3238.speaker: Award recipients of the Africa Prosperity Champions Awards
a3238.name: Award recipients of the Africa Prosperity Champions Awards
a3238.speech: Registered their pleasure to Mr. Gabby Asare Otchere-Darko, the founder and executive chairman of the Africa Prosperity Network, for the honour done them, and pledged to continue in their various endeavours which led to the recognition and to continue to spearhead the transformation agenda of the African continent in their individual sectors of activity to achieve the prosperity of Africa and all her peoples.

a3238.speaker: Dr. Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma, former Chairperson of the African Union Commission and Chairperson of the Africa Prosperity Network Advisory Council
a3238.name: Dr. Nkosazana Dlamini-Zuma
a3238.title: former Chairperson of the African Union Commission and Chairperson of the Africa Prosperity Network Advisory Council
a3238.speech: Remarked in her welcoming address at the official opening ceremony of the Africa Prosperity Dialogue on Monday, January 30, 2025, that the "APD is like Africa's magnetic force, and the time for talk is over; now is the moment for decisive action."

a3238.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a3238.name: John Dramani Mahama
a3238.title: President of Ghana
a3238.speech: Said in his remarks at the 2025 Africa Prosperity Dialogue on February 1, 2025, at the Accra International Conference Centre: "Ghana is proud to be the host of this important dialogue series, and it will continue to enjoy my full support to make subsequent events even greater. This congress is a testament to our collective commitment to unlocking Africa's full potential and ensuring that our continent takes its rightful place in the global economic system."

a3253.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a3253.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
a3253.title: President of Tanzania
a3253.speech: In a powerful address closing the 12th Parliament, highlighted her administration's achievements throughout her tenure.

a3253.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a3253.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
a3253.title: President of Tanzania
a3253.speech: Noted significant progress in domestic revenue collection, with tax revenues rising from 1.51tri/- in 2020 to 3.09tri/- in 2025 - an increase of 104 percent, the country's overall annual revenue growing from 24.06tri/- to 34.61tri/-, enabling a reduction in dependence on foreign aid and loans from -2.6 percent to -3.4 percent ; Addressed the growth in exports, with the value of exported goods increasing from 6.39bn US dollars to USD 8.7bn - an increase of 2.31bn US dollars or 100 percent, attributed to higher international prices for key cash crops such as pigeon peas and cotton ; Reported a decline in inflation from 5.6 percent in 2020 to an average of 3.0 percent in 2025, contributing to lower living costs including a drop in the price of sugar from 3,000/- to 2,717/- per kilogram.

a3253.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a3253.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
a3253.title: President of Tanzania
a3253.speech: Announced the appointment of 83 new judges and the recruitment of 1,153 magistrates and court staff, measures which have helped reduce case backlogs and expedite access to justice across the country.

a3253.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a3253.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
a3253.title: President of Tanzania
a3253.speech: Revealed that 328 new health centers have been constructed, raising the total from 1,254 to 1,582 - a 26.2 percent increase, that 2,006 new doctors have been recruited, and that the number of anesthesiologists has grown from just 36 to over 200, representing a 455 percent increase and marking a significant boost in medical service delivery.

a3253.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a3253.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
a3253.title: President of Tanzania
a3253.speech: Highlighted that over 1,220 students have benefited from the Samia Scholarship, which has disbursed 7.2bn/-, that daily student allowances have been increased from 7,500/- to 10,000/-, and that the HESLB fund has grown from 464bn/- to 786bn/-, benefiting 229,000 students in total; 2,381 new primary schools have been built, increasing the number from 18,152 to 20,533, and the number of secondary school students has risen by two million due to a boost in the free education budget from 312bn/- to 796.58bn/- - an increase of 155 percent.

a3253.speaker: Samia Suluhu Hassan, President of Tanzania
a3253.name: Samia Suluhu Hassan
a3253.title: President of Tanzania
a3253.speech: Concluded her speech by focusing on the security sector, where the government has constructed 6,064 new houses for security officers, hired 16,009 new officers, and built 472 new police stations; she emphasized that these actions have boosted morale within the security forces and enhanced the safety of citizens and their property.

a3259.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB) Group / 2025 African Economic Outlook (report)
a3259.name: African Development Bank (AfDB) Group / 2025 African Economic Outlook (report)
a3259.speech: Says Malawi's economic outlook remains positive despite downside risks; the bank projects real gross domestic product to rise to three percent in 2025 and 3.8 percent in 2026, driven by a recovery in agriculture and tourism, alongside gains from mining investments. Reads the outlook in part: "On the demand side, growth will be bolstered by a rebound in exports and improved real incomes, supporting consumer spending and investment. Inflation is expected to decline to 23.8 percent by 2026, reflecting better food supply conditions." ; The group said key risks to the outlook include US reciprocal trade tariffs and aid cuts, delays in resolving the debt crisis and climate-related shocks, which could undermine fiscal stability, infrastructure investments and agricultural recovery: "Addressing these risks will require accelerated structural reforms, strengthened fiscal discipline, and enhanced climate resilience measures to sustain the growth momentum."

a3259.speaker: Kevin Chika Urama, AfDB group vice-president and chief economist
a3259.name: Kevin Chika Urama
a3259.title: AfDB group vice-president and chief economist
a3259.speech: Observed that persistent inflationary pressures, high interest rates, debt service costs and debt refinancing risks, continued commodity dependence and price volatility in commodity markets, and increased climate shocks continue to pose headwinds to African economies: "And more recently, geopolitical tensions, trade policy uncertainty, regional conflicts and political instability have become more prominent. While these headwinds, including the recent escalation in trade tariffs illustrate the vulnerabilities inherent in over-reliance on foreign trade and global value chains, they also present opportunities for African countries to deepen intra-regional trade, strengthen economic diversification and regional economic integration, and deepen efforts in strengthening institutions, governance and rule of law."

a3259.speaker: Simplex Chithyola-Banda, Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs, Malawi
a3259.name: Simplex Chithyola-Banda
a3259.title: Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs, Malawi
a3259.speech: Conceded in the 2025/26 Budget Statement that since the current administration assumed office in 2020, it has been navigating through various economic turbulences: "As such, the economic landscape has not evolved as anticipated, with persistent pressures on key indicators such as economic growth, exchange rates, inflation and structural shifts in trade and production."

a3362.speaker: Amnesty International (report)
a3362.name: Amnesty International (report)
a3362.speech: Cited by the coalition's statement as reporting that at least 10,217 Nigerians have been killed in violent attacks over the past two years — figures they described as "wartime levels of slaughter" despite the country being officially at peace.

a3362.speaker: Coalition of prominent Nigerian leaders (joint statement)
a3362.name: Coalition of prominent Nigerian leaders (joint statement)
a3362.speech: Issued a joint statement raising concerns over the country's worsening security crisis, warning that Nigeria is "bleeding" and risks sliding into chaos unless urgent, coordinated action is taken; the statement highlighted figures from states hardest hit by violence — Benue alone has recorded nearly 6,900 deaths with over 450,000 people displaced, while Plateau has lost more than 2,600 lives to attacks that have destroyed farms, poisoned water sources, and displaced entire communities; in Zamfara, at least 638 villages have been razed, with residents now forced to pay criminal levies under threats of mass killings ; condemned what they described as "a dangerous national silence" and the failure of the Nigerian state to maintain its monopoly on the legitimate use of force, warning that farmer-herder disputes, once localised, have now morphed into sectarian wars fuelled by military-grade weapons, impunity, and a collapse of governance at community levels.

a3362.speaker: Coalition of prominent Nigerian leaders (joint statement)
a3362.name: Coalition of prominent Nigerian leaders (joint statement)
a3362.speech: Drawing lessons from other nations such as Colombia, Rwanda, and Northern Ireland, urged Nigeria to confront its deep ethnic and religious divides through reforms, reconciliation, and inclusive governance; rejecting ethnic scapegoating, stressed that perpetrators of violence are Nigerians from different communities, driven by systemic problems of poverty, injustice, arms proliferation, and weak governance, and called for justice to be "blind to identity": "We must resist the temptation to blame this violence on one group alone. As recent revelations in Katsina, Anambra, Benue and Plateau have shown that, while some of the attackers are foreigners with local collaborators, many of the attackers are Nigerians, sons of the soil, from various communities, who have abandoned kinship for criminality." ; "This is a Nigerian problem with Nigerian faces. The challenge is not ethnic, but systemic: poverty, arms proliferation, impunity, injustice, and the erosion of local governance. We must lift the veil of stereotypes and deal with the truth: criminals come from every group: justice must be blind to identity."

a3362.speaker: Coalition of prominent Nigerian leaders (joint statement)
a3362.name: Coalition of prominent Nigerian leaders (joint statement)
a3362.speech: Proposed the urgent creation of a Presidential Task Force on National Security with extraordinary powers to coordinate intelligence, disarm armed groups, reintegrate displaced populations, and publish quarterly reports on arrests and prosecutions to rebuild public trust: "We refuse to be silent accomplices.
