We call on the Presidency, National Assembly, Governors, traditional rulers, religious leaders, security chiefs, civil society, and every Nigerian of conscience: let us forge a new path." ; "We propose urgently creating a Presidential Task Force on National Security, with extraordinary powers and a clear mandate to coordinate and execute emergency measures to halt the violence. This Taskforce should work directly with the National Security Adviser (NSA) and all relevant security, intelligence, and humanitarian agencies." ; demanded operationalising community-based early warning systems and rapid response frameworks, and implementing a disarmament and reintegration programme for conflict zones, particularly in the North East, North Central and North West ; "Driving accountability through quarterly public security reports, disclosing arrests, prosecutions, and progress made- thereby rebuilding public trust and strengthening civilian oversight." ; "The Presidential Taskforce must be time-bound, results-driven, and composed of experienced security professionals, non-partisan Nigerians of unquestionable integrity, and war-time decision makers who are bold enough to use their mandate responsibly and transparently." ; "The body should report directly to the President but operate independently of political pressures. These are unusual times, they require unusual but constitutional measures."

a3362.speaker: Coalition of prominent Nigerian leaders (joint statement)
a3362.name: Coalition of prominent Nigerian leaders (joint statement)
a3362.speech: Warned that Nigeria stands on a "knife-edge," and that history will judge not the bandits but those in authority who failed to act decisively: "Nigeria stands on a knife-edge. Whether we tip into chaos or climb toward peace depends on what we do next. If Rwanda, Colombia, and Northern Ireland can emerge from darker abysses, so can we, if our leaders, across the villa, government houses and Assembly, our palaces, pulpits, and barracks, take the more challenging road of reconciliation, justice, and reform." ; "The right of every Nigerian child - in Bokkos, Gwoza, Maru or Yelwata - to grow up without fear is not negotiable." ; "History will not judge the bandits. It will judge us who had the power to protect, and either rose to this moment or shrank from it. May God grant us the courage to act, and may He heal our land."

a3393.speaker: Liberian Senate
a3393.name: Liberian Senate
a3393.speech: Has mandated its Committees on Ways, Means, Finance and Budget and Foreign Affairs to invite several relevant ministries - Foreign Affairs, Finance and Development Planning, Health, Education and Agriculture - on the suspension of Foreign Aid by America, so that the government entities will provide solutions to the impacts of the recent foreign aid suspension by the United States of America.

a3393.speaker: Senators Amara Konneh, Edwin Snowe, Gbehzohngar Findley, Abraham Darius Dillon and Augustine Chea of Gbarpolu, Bomi, Grand Bassa, Montserrado and Sinoe Counties (joint communication)
a3393.name: Senators Amara Konneh
a3393.title: Edwin Snowe, Gbehzohngar Findley, Abraham Darius Dillon and Augustine Chea of Gbarpolu, Bomi, Grand Bassa, Montserrado and Sinoe Counties (joint communication)
a3393.speech: The Senators believed that the United States' suspension of foreign aid presents considerable challenges to the nation's Public Health, Education, and Agriculture sectors, as such, there is a need to find a solution.

a3454.speaker: Saint Jerome Koffi, project officer at the regional directorate of AFD and chairman of the organizing committee
a3454.name: Saint Jerome Koffi
a3454.title: project officer at the regional directorate of AFD and chairman of the organizing committee
a3454.speech: Specified that the teams are composed exclusively of staff members of the various participating institutions.

a3454.speaker: Lionel Yondo, AFD Regional Director for the Gulf of Guinea
a3454.name: Lionel Yondo
a3454.title: AFD Regional Director for the Gulf of Guinea
a3454.speech: Underlined the importance of this event: "This tournament is of paramount importance insofar as it allows our colleagues, who are used to crossing paths at the office or in meetings, to experience a moment of conviviality and to bring their families together. It is also an opportunity for all the partners supporting Cote d'Ivoire in its development to fraternize and strengthen their closeness. We fully share the values of social cohesion and fraternity that sport promotes."

a3496.speaker: Virgina Patrico Murio, Programme Officer with the National Association for Self-Sustainable Development (ANDA)
a3496.name: Virgina Patrico Murio
a3496.title: Programme Officer with the National Association for Self-Sustainable Development (ANDA)
a3496.speech: Explained: "We work with WFP [World Food Programme] and FAO [Food and Agriculture Organization] to ensure assistance reaches people in Macossa's communities. As a local organization, we have a deep understanding of the people, their life and things that happen in the community. Our knowledge of the local culture, our proximity to the community and the good relationship with the district authorities are key factors that allow us to achieve good results." ; "The community is effectively involved in the whole process; they play a leading role and make decisions on how the assistance should be conducted."

a3496.speaker: Virgina Patrico Murio, Programme Officer with the National Association for Self-Sustainable Development (ANDA)
a3496.name: Virgina Patrico Murio
a3496.title: Programme Officer with the National Association for Self-Sustainable Development (ANDA)
a3496.speech: Explained: "From the time we are able to identify issues in the community and provide solutions, we feel empowered and that our role goes beyond just helping UN partners; rather, we are leading the response ourselves, as long as we have the necessary funding. Therefore, capacity-building would help to strengthen local organizations and involve them in the response."

a3496.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a3496.name: Government of Mozambique
a3496.speech: According to the Government, these actions are also transforming how communities prepare for drought and minimize its devastating impact before it reaches crisis levels.

a3496.speaker: Antonio Dinis, District Administrator for Macossa, Manica Province
a3496.name: Antonio Dinis
a3496.title: District Administrator for Macossa, Manica Province
a3496.speech: "If the UN and other partners had not responded quickly to the impact of drought in our district, the situation could have worsened and probably by now we could be reporting deaths."

a3496.speaker: Lourenco Lindonde, Secretary of State of Manica Province
a3496.name: Lourenco Lindonde
a3496.title: Secretary of State of Manica Province
a3496.speech: "It's important to work together to mitigate the impact of drought in our province and beyond, because working in isolation we may not achieve the desired results."

a3496.speaker: Paola Emerson, Head of OCHA Mozambique
a3496.name: Paola Emerson
a3496.title: Head of OCHA Mozambique
a3496.speech: "We have been collaborating effectively with the different partners, and we look forward to having more efficiency as we continue doing joint assessments and monitoring."

a3626.speaker: CDC executive council
a3626.name: CDC executive council
a3626.speech: Reportedly disapproving of the anti-Koffa campaign, is considering strong repercussions, including suspensions and possible expulsions, for party members involved in the effort.

a3626.speaker: Acarous Gray, former CDC Representative (Facebook Live)
a3626.name: Acarous Gray
a3626.title: former CDC Representative (Facebook Live)
a3626.speech: Revealed that the CDC executive council is firmly against the move to unseat Koffa and has decided to suspend some of its lawmakers pending investigation.

a3626.speaker: Ivar Jones, Margibi County Representative
a3626.name: Ivar Jones
a3626.title: Margibi County Representative
a3626.speech: Reportedly stated he would accept any suspension and undergo investigation by the council for his role in the effort to remove Koffa.

a3626.speaker: Acarous Gray, former CDC Representative (Facebook Live)
a3626.name: Acarous Gray
a3626.title: former CDC Representative (Facebook Live)
a3626.speech: Appealed to his CDC colleagues to abandon the campaign against Koffa and "return home as heroes" ; expressed particular disappointment in Deputy Speaker Thomas Fallah, a former Koffa ally, for joining the majority bloc against the Speaker, calling Fallah's move "dangerous" and potentially damaging to his political ambitions.

a3626.speaker: Acarous Gray, former CDC Representative (Facebook Live)
a3626.name: Acarous Gray
a3626.title: former CDC Representative (Facebook Live)
a3626.speech: Alleged that influential figures including Vice President Jeremiah Koung, former House Speaker J. Alex Tyler, Senator Prince Moye, and Senator Emmanuel Nuquay were financially backing the push to unseat Koffa; added that Sirleaf Tyler, brother of Alex Tyler, allegedly contributed US$500,000 to support the effort, and that Boakai loyalists within key government institutions, including the Ministries of Finance and Transport, as well as state-owned enterprises, are facilitating the funding ; "If Boakai isn't involved, then his own administration is undermining him" ; urged Boakai to investigate and bring transparency to the matter given allegations that officials from the Executive are siphoning funds from line ministries to "sponsor chaos in the Legislature."

a3626.speaker: Acarous Gray, former CDC Representative (Facebook Live)
a3626.name: Acarous Gray
a3626.title: former CDC Representative (Facebook Live)
a3626.speech: Cited House Rule 48.6, suggesting that any complaint against Koffa would be invalid due to procedural timing restrictions: complaints must be filed within a year of an alleged violation and would be barred from consideration in the current term.

a3626.speaker: Justice Yarmie Quiqui Gbeisay, Supreme Court of Liberia (ruling)
a3626.name: Justice Yarmie Quiqui Gbeisay
a3626.title: Supreme Court of Liberia (ruling)
a3626.speech: Declined Speaker Koffa's request for a writ of prohibition against the majority bloc.

a3626.speaker: J. Fonati Koffa, Speaker of the House of Representatives (court filing)
a3626.name: J. Fonati Koffa
a3626.title: Speaker of the House of Representatives (court filing)
a3626.speech: Had filed the writ, claiming that the bloc's attempts to bypass his authority by holding separate sessions in the Joint Chambers without his permission set a dangerous precedent.

a3626.speaker: Office of the President of Liberia / Ministry of State for Presidential Affairs (official letter dated November 8, 2024)
a3626.name: Office of the President of Liberia / Ministry of State for Presidential Affairs (official letter dated November 8
a3626.speech: Released an official statement distancing the Executive Branch from the House drama and expressed its commitment to maintaining the independence of Liberia's government branches: "The President regards the evolving situation with the utmost urgency and is unwavering about upholding the sanctity of the 'three separate but coordinate branches' of government." The letter emphasized that Boakai is seeking legal counsel to fully comprehend the implications of the Supreme Court ruling.

a3626.speaker: Dr. Robtel Neajai Pailey, Liberian scholar and activist (open letter published in the Daily Observer)
a3626.name: Dr. Robtel Neajai Pailey
a3626.title: Liberian scholar and activist (open letter published in the Daily Observer)
a3626.speech: Lambasted the majority bloc for allegedly "hijacking the legislative process": "We elected you to represent us well, make good laws (not break them) and provide oversight of the executive and judiciary. Instead, you have hijacked the legislative process and forsaken your own House Rules and Procedures. Nowhere does it say you have authority to hold alternate sessions in the joint chambers, regardless of implicit judicial approval."

a3662.speaker: Bret Baier, Fox News anchor
a3662.name: Bret Baier
a3662.title: Fox News anchor
a3662.speech: Asked Felix Tshisekedi, the president of the Democratic Republic of Congo, how his government would balance continued ties with the United States, including the negotiation of a critical minerals deal, with its deepening relationship with China.

a3662.speaker: Felix Tshisekedi, President of the Democratic Republic of Congo
a3662.name: Felix Tshisekedi
a3662.title: President of the Democratic Republic of Congo
a3662.speech: Responded that China's influence is not so much "waxing" in Africa as America's influence is "waning" ; pointed out that the DRC would be "very happy" to see a renewed US commercial presence there.

a3662.speaker: Gallup poll published last year
a3662.name: Gallup poll published last year
a3662.speech: Showed that, for the first time, China's approval rating in Africa (58%) had surpassed that of the US (56%).

a3662.speaker: Persistent reports (cited)
a3662.name: Persistent reports (cited)
a3662.speech: That the Trump administration plans to reduce the number of US embassies and consulates in Africa.

a3662.speaker: Studies (cited)
a3662.name: Studies (cited)
a3662.speech: Have shown that trade with the US increases value-added production, labor productivity, and labor demand in Africa.

a3662.speaker: African trade ministers
a3662.name: African trade ministers
a3662.speech: Have agreed to fast-track policies that will promote trade within the continent, as well as diversify exports in order to reduce their countries' dependence on particular foreign markets.

a3725.speaker: Ezekiel Kamwaga, scholar of African politics
a3725.name: Ezekiel Kamwaga
a3725.title: scholar of African politics
a3725.speech: Says America’s greatness and global dominance depended on two kinds of power it holds: military power that enabled it to send troops to quell unrest in various nations, and economic power that enabled it to have numerous agencies giving aid to nations and communities around the world; says these are what identified America, earned it respect, made it a friend to many and the ruler of the world; says the steps the nation is now taking strip America of the reputation, strength and respect it holds among many nations, leaving it only with the status of wealth, because its former allies will no longer be persuaded to respect America since they get nothing from it ; “When you remove the US Agency for International Development (USAID), you remove the strength that was helping you to continue to be trusted and loved” ; says nations were compelled to trust America because it was a help in treating millions of patients suffering from various diseases ; “Now America will no longer be trusted. To a large extent he is destroying the nature and the dominance he has had for more than 80 years.”

a3725.speaker: Dr Conrad Masabo, political science scholar at the University of Dodoma (Udom)
a3725.name: Dr Conrad Masabo
a3725.title: political science scholar at the University of Dodoma (Udom)
a3725.speech: Said there is a need to understand how America became the world’s leader; says the status America has now was built by the way it took part at the end of the First and Second World Wars, and that its other strength comes from its firmness in defence and military matters and not from giving aid as many think; says for America to cease being the world’s leader, other countries must stop depending on it for defence, in the sense of sending its troops and equipment ; “As we speak, only three countries have manufactured fighter jets: America, Russia and China” ; explains that because of this reality, European countries have no way of ceasing to be dependent on America, especially on defence matters; says it is only developing countries that depend on American aid to survive from day to day, while others depend on it for defence; says the big financial and civil organisations including the United Nations (UN) were founded on American philosophies and depend on that nation for contributions; explains that China, by its policies, is not ready to carry the responsibility America was carrying because that country does not want to invest in war ; “Apart from the war against Vietnam, their civil wars and the one against Japan, China has never fought any other war, so it does not like war” ; says America likes war because it builds its economy through it, by selling weapons ; “In war, America benefits by selling weapons, so it sees itself as gaining from that. Today if people are frightened they will buy weapons to strengthen themselves” ; says that like China, Russia too has no intention of being the world’s ruler and even its attacks on Ukraine aim to make that country ungovernable; says America will lose the power to rule the world in the diplomatic and human rights context, but it continues to have power because of its military, so it will remain the ruler.

a3725.speaker: Ansbert Ngurumo, veteran journalist living outside Tanzania
a3725.name: Ansbert Ngurumo
a3725.title: veteran journalist living outside Tanzania
a3725.speech: Says what the US President Donald Trump is doing aims to prove that his nation has a voice and the ability to do and destroy what it wants; says every tactic Trump is now using emphasises America’s greatness and that it is the leading nation ; “Here he is proving to his voters that America has a big voice and the ability to do and destroy what it wants, and that it proves itself to be the leader, and that is why when it does this people cry” ; says that although the decision taken is hard, it pleases and benefits Americans because it saves a lot of taxpayers’ money that was going to do other work in other people’s projects ; “Because Trump is a businessman, his interpretation of life is money, so everything including his politics he does in money terms” ; says what America is now doing adds more strength to that nation in being respected and building influence with voters and the world in general ; “He is shaking other nations so that they kneel before him; he wants them to agree so that he gives less than what he is now giving as his contribution, and that other nations increase the amount they give, because he sees his nation being exploited” ; says, however, that what Trump is doing is creating many future enemies for America, something that will harm that nation ; “Those who built America into a nation that gives aid intended to connect it with world politics. What Trump is doing is contrary to that intention; true, for now it will benefit America and he personally will build influence among Americans, but he is building enmity with the world and its effects will be seen later.”

a3725.speaker: Ibrahim Rabhi, international politics analyst
a3725.name: Ibrahim Rabhi
a3725.title: international politics analyst
a3725.speech: Says America already removed itself long ago from the position of leading the world; according to Rabhi, what remains in that nation is the power of force that has cowed the world for a long time; says the nation has left that position because it has lost the qualification of being a leader, owing to the continuing conflicts in the Middle East and its practice of repeatedly imposing sanctions, things not expected of a leader; explains that America has now decided to shed the skin it had long been hiding in of promoting democracy, freedom and rights, and instead promotes its own private interests ; “By doing what it is continuing to do, it gives a great opening for other nations seeking the chance to lead the world to get that chance” ; says this step will also harm America itself by losing important allies it previously had ; “For example, now the European Union is thinking about their security for themselves and not thinking about their security on America’s back; all this is because America is no longer the leader.”

a3785.speaker: Interim administration of Tigray Regional State
a3785.name: Interim administration of Tigray Regional State
a3785.speech: Has said it will work aggressively on public relations and communication in the region to separate the people from the TPLF, since the people of Tigray have been very close and highly attached to the TPLF ; said it has finalized its charter to re-establish new Regional and Zone cabinet structures, while Woreda councils and Kebele administration will continue.

a3785.speaker: Mulu Nega, CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a3785.name: Mulu Nega
a3785.title: CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a3785.speech: “The Tigray people have been hostage of the TPLF for many years. One of the important work the interim administration will be involved in is the rehabilitation work on cooperating with the federal government to ensure justice and good governance widens the political space in the region by involving all political parties” ; “The political space in the region has been very narrow. So we will open up this and invite all political parties, groups and individuals to operate by respecting the rule of law” ; noted that the TPLF will not be allowed to participate in the new administration, since high officials and executive bodies are engaged in the crime and the so-called illegal election, and that in collaboration with other relevant government bodies the administration will take steps to address the situation that threatens the constitutional order in Tigray Regional State ; “The establishment of the interim administration aims to ensuring the benefits of the People of Tigray and sustain lasting peace by restructuring the preceding administration system.”

a3785.speaker: Mulu Nega, CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a3785.name: Mulu Nega
a3785.title: CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a3785.speech: Said in his media briefing on Thursday that provisional administration will be instituted in the areas liberated from the TPLF ; noted that the new administration will establish a task force to investigate the case of individuals in custody in the Tigray region, and that the Tigrayan people have been suffering from lack of justice and good governance, adding that the interim administration will work to create an enabling situation whereby these problems could be tackled.

a3785.speaker: Mulu Nega, CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a3785.name: Mulu Nega
a3785.title: CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a3785.speech: Said the interim administration will discharge its responsibility in facilitating credible and participatory elections to be held in Tigray Regional State: “Making smooth transition and conducting free and legal election are the main targets of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State,” adding that the people of Tigray have been coerced into unfair and illegal elections by the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) for years ; said the immediate action will be resuming social services not properly functioning at the moment, including education and health, in collaboration with the federal government, sector ministries and other stakeholders.

a3785.speaker: Mulu Nega, CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a3785.name: Mulu Nega
a3785.title: CEO of the Interim Administration of Tigray Regional State
a3785.speech: Regarding the relation with Eritrea: “We will try to restore peace and stability with neighboring regions and Eritrea. There is some mistrust. So our task is to restore peace and stability within Tigray as well as with neighboring regions and the Eritrean government.”

a3785.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopian government spokesman
a3785.name: Redwan Hussein
a3785.title: Ethiopian government spokesman
a3785.speech: “Our defense forces are moving forward and closing in on Mekelle,” he told reporters. “There are a number of towns that have fallen,” he added.

a3785.speaker: Redwan Hussein, Ethiopian government spokesman
a3785.name: Redwan Hussein
a3785.title: Ethiopian government spokesman
a3785.speech: Informed the Capital newspaper that countries, including the United Nations, were evacuating their citizens and staff from the Tigray region, and that hundreds of foreign aid workers have left Tigray through the borders of Afar ; said the regional government is protecting them from Mekelle to the border of Afar State through their satellite communications, and that all organizations must provide a list of people to be evacuated and ensure that they are not wanted for crime ; said the government is seeking better conditions for humanitarian assistance to the United Nations to alleviate living conditions in the Tigray region, and that the government has organized two groups of fact-finding missions to assess the situation on the ground on both the western and east southern parts of the region to find which way is easiest to supply humanitarian assistance, with a plan to bring back migrants from neighboring countries.

a3924.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3924.title: Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.speech: Stated that HIV infections have been declining in recent years, with only 1.3 million new cases recorded in 2023, a 60% decline since the peak of the virus in 1995.

a3924.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3924.title: Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.speech: Said that with the US President's announcement freezing all foreign assistance for 90 days, authorities estimate that by 2029 there could be 8.7 million people infected with HIV, a tenfold increase in disease-related deaths (to 6.3 million) and 3.4 million more orphaned children: "We will see an increase in this disease", speaking from Uganda ; "It will cost lives if the United States Government does not change its mind and maintains its leadership", adding that it is not her place to criticise any government policy.

a3924.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3924.title: Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.speech: Pleaded with the Trump administration not to cut the funding abruptly, which she said resulted in "panic, fear and confusion" in many of the African countries hardest hit by AIDS; recounted that in one county in Kenya 550 HIV professionals were immediately dismissed, while thousands of others in Ethiopia were dismissed, leaving health authorities unable to track the epidemic; observed that the loss of United States funding for HIV programmes in some countries was catastrophic, with external funding, mainly American, representing around 90% of their programmes; detailed that almost 400 million dollars go to countries such as Uganda, Mozambique and Tanzania ; "We can work with the Americans on how to reduce their contribution, if that is what they want."

a3924.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3924.title: Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.speech: Described the American withdrawal from global efforts against HIV as the second biggest crisis the sector has ever faced — after the years of delay it took for poor countries to obtain the life-saving antiretrovirals long available in rich countries.

a3924.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3924.title: Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.speech: Noted that the loss of American support comes at another critical moment, with the arrival of what she called "a magic prevention tool" known as lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injection shown to offer complete protection against HIV in women and which worked almost as well for men; said widespread use of it, in addition to other interventions to halt HIV, could help end the disease as a public health problem within the next five years; said it is sold as Sunlenca and was developed by the American company Gilead ; said international aid "helped an American company innovate, to create something that will earn them millions and millions, but at the same time will prevent new infections in the rest of the world", stating that the funding freeze makes no economic sense ; "We appeal to the United States Government to review this, to understand that this is mutually beneficial", noting that foreign assistance represents less than 1% of the overall United States budget: "Why would it need to be so disruptive for that 1%?"

a3924.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.name: Winnie Byanyima
a3924.title: Executive Director of UNAIDS (in an interview with the Associated Press)
a3924.speech: Said that so far no other country or donor has come forward to fill the void that will be left by the loss of American aid, but that she plans to visit several European capitals to speak with global leaders: "People will die because life-saving tools have been taken away from them" ; "I have not yet heard of any European country that has committed to stepping in, but I know they are listening and trying to see where they can step in, because they care about rights, about humanity."

a3924.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3924.name: Donald Trump
a3924.title: US President
a3924.speech: Announced that the United States would freeze all foreign assistance for 90 days.

a3936.speaker: Members of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement in Opposition (SPLM/IO)
a3936.name: Members of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement in Opposition (SPLM/IO)
a3936.speech: Say that since Tuesday, soldiers of the South Sudanese army have surrounded Machar’s home in Juba.

a3936.speaker: Analysts (unnamed)
a3936.name: Analysts (unnamed)
a3936.speech: Said the 2018 peace agreement is now under threat from renewed tensions between Kiir and Machar; analysts said tensions in Juba are likely to keep delaying crucial tasks ahead for the young country, including the signing of a permanent constitution and the holding of elections.

a3936.speaker: Machar’s SPLM/IO
a3936.name: Machar’s SPLM/IO
a3936.speech: Opposed the Tumaini Peace Initiative process, saying it could affect some of the terms agreed in the 2018 peace deal.

a3936.speaker: Human Rights Watch (HRW)
a3936.name: Human Rights Watch (HRW)
a3936.speech: Identified a group involved in the Nasir County fighting as an “armed youth militia”; said rumours of a forced disarmament plan of other groups by government troops had caused concern within the local armed group, but that it remains unclear what exactly started the fighting; said the South Sudanese army attacked positions of the unnamed armed youth group, leading to a series of deadly confrontations.

a3936.speaker: Radio Tamazuj station
a3936.name: Radio Tamazuj station
a3936.speech: At least five civilians have been killed as a result of the fighting, according to the station.

a3936.speaker: United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a3936.name: United Nations Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS)
a3936.speech: Reported that a peacekeeper was wounded in the clashes; added that the warring parties, which it also did not name, used “heavy weaponry” and that fighting had also been reported in Western Equatoria State in the southwestern part of the country.

a3936.speaker: Michael Makuei Lueth, South Sudan’s Information Minister
a3936.name: Michael Makuei Lueth
a3936.title: South Sudan’s Information Minister
a3936.speech: At a news conference this week, blamed the White Army, a Nuer armed group operating in Upper Nile that he said had been the first to attack army garrisons in Nasir County, and said that group was working with the SPLM/IO. “We are calling on them to control their forces. … The government is in full control of the situation, and we are in the process of addressing the situation in Nasir,” he said.

a3936.speaker: Reuters news agency
a3936.name: Reuters news agency
a3936.speech: Reported that Peacebuilding Minister Stephen Par Kuol was released early on Friday.

a3936.speaker: Pal Mai Deng, spokesman for the SPLM/IO party and minister for water resources
a3936.name: Pal Mai Deng
a3936.title: spokesman for the SPLM/IO party and minister for water resources
a3936.speech: In a statement on Tuesday, said Kiir’s recent actions had “eroded trust and confidence” among the parties to the peace agreement. “This [Kiir’s] action violates the Revitalised Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan. … This act puts the entire agreement at risk,” Deng said.

a3936.speaker: William Ruto, Kenyan President
a3936.name: William Ruto
a3936.title: Kenyan President
a3936.speech: Acknowledged the escalating tensions in a statement on Thursday and revealed that he’d spoken to both Kiir and Machar. “I implored both leaders to engage in dialogue towards fostering peace in the country, even as the region works towards the stabilisation of South Sudan under IGAD’s Strategic Framework,” Ruto said. “I also informed the two leaders that regional consultations are underway to determine the best path forward for the situation in South Sudan.”

a3936.speaker: IGAD country representatives in Juba (joint statement)
a3936.name: IGAD country representatives in Juba (joint statement)
a3936.speech: Said they were alarmed at the Nasir County violence, which they said threatens to undermine gains from the peace deal and exacerbate an already dire humanitarian situation. “We call upon all the parties and their affiliate groups to immediately cease hostilities and exercise maximum restraint. We emphasise the paramount importance of upholding the Permanent Ceasefire and adhering to the provisions of the R-ARCSS.”

a3936.speaker: Embassies of Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, the United Kingdom, the United States and the European Union (joint statement)
a3936.name: Embassies of Canada
a3936.title: France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, the United Kingdom, the United States and the European Union (joint statement)
a3936.speech: “[We] deplore the hostilities in Upper Nile State which included significant loss of lives. We are also concerned by reports of detentions of senior military and civilian officials. We join our IGAD counterparts in calling for immediate cessation of hostilities and for all parties and their affiliates to exercise maximum restraint.”

a3936.speaker: Kiir’s government
a3936.name: Kiir’s government
a3936.speech: Postponed elections originally planned for December, citing funding challenges and “unpreparedness”.

a3936.speaker: Mohammed Akot, pro-democracy activist
a3936.name: Mohammed Akot
a3936.title: pro-democracy activist
a3936.speech: Criticised both the SPLM and SPLM/IO for failing to make progress in the peace process because of “a lack of political will”; described the recent arrests as a “clear violation” by the ruling party that threatens the 2018 peace deal. “If the disputes are not resolved, particularly in Nasir County, and if the parties do not commit to fully implementing all security arrangements, the risk of renewed conflict will remain, threatening the country’s stability. Genuine political commitment is now required to salvage the peace process,” he told Al Jazeera.

a3936.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) report
a3936.name: World Food Programme (WFP) report
a3936.speech: Issued a report this week saying it faces a $412m funding shortfall to address the country’s humanitarian crisis, caused by years of conflict, climate change and general economic deprivation; according to the WFP, more than 7.6 million people are facing food shortages in the country while one in every four children is malnourished.

a3936.speaker: International Rescue Committee (IRC)
a3936.name: International Rescue Committee (IRC)
a3936.speech: Said last week that its work providing food to malnourished children could cease after the US cut foreign aid worldwide; said it has assisted 1.5 million people in the country since it started working in then-southern Sudan in 1989.

a4063.speaker: New research published in Biophysical Journal (study)
a4063.name: New research published in Biophysical Journal (study)
a4063.speech: Found that face masks could potentially lower the severity of Covid-19 infection and could help explain why the wearing of masks is linked to lower disease severity in people infected with SARS-CoV-2, possibly because hydration of the respiratory tract benefits the immune system; researchers assessed four common types of mask and found that all four increased the amounts of humidity in the inhaled air, with the thick cotton mask producing the highest levels.

a4063.speaker: Dr Adriaan Bax, lead author of the study
a4063.name: Dr Adriaan Bax
a4063.title: lead author of the study
a4063.speech: "The increased level of humidity is something most mask-wearers probably felt without being able to recognise it, and without realising that this humidity might actually be good for them" ; "We found that face masks strongly increase the humidity in the inhaled air and propose that the resulting hydration of the respiratory tract could be responsible for the documented finding that links lower Covid-19 disease severity to wearing a mask. High levels of humidity have been shown to mitigate [the] severity of the flu, and it may be applicable to the severity of Covid-19 through a similar mechanism."

a4063.speaker: The researchers
a4063.name: The researchers
a4063.speech: Point out that their study had a limited focus in that it did not look at which masks are most effective against inhalation or transmission of the virus.

a4063.speaker: Experts
a4063.name: Experts
a4063.speech: Say that high levels of humidity can limit the spread of a virus to the lungs by promoting mucociliary clearance (MCC), a defence mechanism that removes mucus and potentially harmful particles within the mucus from the lungs ; also say that high levels of humidity can strengthen the immune system by producing special proteins, called interferons, that fight viruses, while low levels of humidity have been shown to impair both MCC and the interferon response.

a4286.speaker: Officials of Turkey and the United States (Washington and Ankara)
a4286.name: Officials of Turkey and the United States (Washington and Ankara)
a4286.speech: The announcement was made by officials of the two countries that the total closure of the border between Turkey and Syria will become a reality in the coming days ; Washington and Ankara have already agreed on this operation.

a4286.speaker: Investigations (unspecified)
a4286.name: Investigations (unspecified)
a4286.speech: Investigations revealed that the jihadists who leave Syria for Europe pass through this route.

a4396.speaker: Amarula, host of the "African Initiative"
a4396.name: Amarula
a4396.title: host of the "African Initiative"
a4396.speech: Talks about the fight against terrorism and about how Russia is helping the Sahel country.

a4403.speaker: Perseus Mlambo, CEO of ChitChat
a4403.name: Perseus Mlambo
a4403.title: CEO of ChitChat
a4403.speech: "We are thrilled to introduce remittances as the latest offering on the ChitChat platform. This feature allows Africans at home and abroad to send money easily and securely. Whether it's a bank deposit to the UK, a mobile wallet transfer to Zimbabwe, or a cash payout in Ghana, we aim to provide a smooth and accessible service for all."

a4506.speaker: Dr Lamien Nieyidouba, programme officer at CORAF (West and Central African Council for Agricultural Research and Development)
a4506.name: Dr Lamien Nieyidouba
a4506.title: programme officer at CORAF (West and Central African Council for Agricultural Research and Development)
a4506.speech: Sought to reassure stakeholders in the face of the suspension of USAID funding: "We never designed this project to depend on a single donor. Several partners are involved and their contributions are brought together in synergy to ensure the implementation of the parks. We benefit from the support of other partners such as the World Bank and Swiss cooperation, which continue to support us," he declared; acknowledging that the situation with USAID undeniably represents a loss of resources, he assured that it does not jeopardise the programme as a whole.

a4506.speaker: Dr Lamien Nieyidouba, programme officer at CORAF
a4506.name: Dr Lamien Nieyidouba
a4506.title: programme officer at CORAF
a4506.speech: Indicated that the organisation is considering seeking the support of local development projects and obtaining their assistance in order to set up demonstrations in their areas of intervention; he acknowledges that "if we want to deploy these parks on a large scale, the costs become more substantial," and appealed to national governments: "We are giving a nod to the authorities: government support would make it possible to extend these actions and reach a larger part of the country," he said.

a4506.speaker: Dr Aliou Faye, researcher at the Senegalese Institute of Agricultural Research (ISRA) and programme coordinator
a4506.name: Dr Aliou Faye
a4506.title: researcher at the Senegalese Institute of Agricultural Research (ISRA) and programme coordinator
a4506.speech: Identified the fundamental problem that, despite significant advances made by agricultural research, notably in collaboration with USAID through the Futures Sustainable Intensification Innovation Lab programme, many innovations remained confined to laboratories without reaching producers; Dr Faye says he developed the I-RICH initiative (Innovation Research Extension Advisory Coordination Hub), a platform dedicated to disseminating research results.

a4506.speaker: Dr Aliou Faye, researcher at the Senegalese Institute of Agricultural Research (ISRA) and programme coordinator
a4506.name: Dr Aliou Faye
a4506.title: researcher at the Senegalese Institute of Agricultural Research (ISRA) and programme coordinator
a4506.speech: "The concrete results testify to the effectiveness of the approach. The new millet variety SL 28 (Senegalese Lines) offers a potential yield of 3.7 tonnes per hectare, compared with less than one tonne for the traditional Sauna 3 variety. With such productivity, a farmer cultivating three hectares could obtain up to 10 tonnes of millet, far beyond the food needs of an average family, thus allowing commercial exploitation and a substantial improvement in income," stressed Dr Faye.

a4506.speaker: Scientific studies, notably several master's theses by agricultural engineers
a4506.name: Scientific studies
a4506.title: notably several master's theses by agricultural engineers
a4506.speech: Have documented and validated the remarkable performance of the innovations presented.

a4506.speaker: Governors of the Senegalese regions concerned
a4506.name: Governors of the Senegalese regions concerned
a4506.speech: At the inaugurations of the various parks, expressed their desire to extend this initiative nationwide.

a4961.speaker: Julius Kanubah, newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.name: Julius Kanubah
a4961.title: newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.speech: Vowed that the "PUL is here to stay for good"; delivering his inaugural address, promised to set up and enforce mechanisms of accountability for all elected officers, chairpersons and members of permanent/standing committees, the support staff, and regional/county coordinators ; said his leadership will conduct constitutional mini-congress to make annual progressive and financial reports at the end of every fiscal year.

a4961.speaker: Julius Kanubah, newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.name: Julius Kanubah
a4961.title: newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.speech: Asserted, on impartial advocacy, "we will work to uphold and enforce ethical standards of journalism aiming to deepen journalistic and media professionalism; responsibly engage the Liberian Government on finding solutions to national issues bordering on the survival of the nation and its people."

a4961.speaker: Julius Kanubah, newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.name: Julius Kanubah
a4961.title: newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.speech: Said constructing the PUL headquarters complex is a priority: "We have had four presidents who promised a headquarters. Today, I wish to announce that we will Establish a Special Resource Mobilization and Project Implementation Committee of credible media, Government and civil society actors for PUL Headquarters construction."

a4961.speaker: Julius Kanubah, newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.name: Julius Kanubah
a4961.title: newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.speech: Said his administration will actively engage media owners, managers, and editors to expand and advance the career and leadership roles of female journalists and media practitioners through the Female Journalists Association of Liberia (FeJAL) to train, build capacity, and seek fellowship opportunities and programs for female journalists.

a4961.speaker: Julius Kanubah, newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.name: Julius Kanubah
a4961.title: newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.speech: On media development: "We will vigorously engage in institutional capacity-building and training programs to ensure the viability and productivity of the Union and its membership; initiate and reactive discussions and negotiations with media owners, managers, editors and media practitioners regarding the Collective Bargaining Agreement dealing with the service of work conditions and health insurance scheme for journalists and media workers; Convene working sessions and panels to reach common understanding regarding the introduction and enforcement of improved salaries of journalists and media workers; Forge good partnerships with the Liberian Government, media development organizations and other partners to improve media economy and institutional context" ; promised also to reactivate and strengthen regional and international networks with journalism and media organizations including FAJ, IFJ, NED, WAJA, CPJ and ALJA, and to strengthen partnership with constituent/affiliate auxiliaries.

a4961.speaker: Julius Kanubah, newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.name: Julius Kanubah
a4961.title: newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.speech: Thanked the United States Government for its continuous support to the media in Liberia through the USAID-funded Media Activity, being implemented by Internews and its network of media alliances ; "We also thank all partners for standing by and with the media. We will knock on your doors in the coming days, weeks, and months."

a4961.speaker: Julius Kanubah, newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.name: Julius Kanubah
a4961.title: newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.speech: Said that under his leadership the PUL will establish and activate one media hub in each of the fourteen counties as sub-chapters of the Union, develop and activate leadership and permanent/standing committee structures of media hubs, and develop and enforce a cost-benefit-sharing arrangement to ensure each media hub is financially/materially empowered from the resources mobilized by the PUL ; said each media hub will conduct monitoring and evaluation of journalistic practices and the operations of the media for the annual awards of county-based and regional journalists in addition to the PUL Annual Awards.

a4961.speaker: Julius Kanubah, newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.name: Julius Kanubah
a4961.title: newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.speech: On auditing the immediate past leadership: "To implement our agenda we will count and enlist your support, resources, ideas, suggestions, recommendations, and criticisms. And as a mark of good leadership in terms of transparently accounting for the transition from one elected and or serving administration to another, we hereby announce that there will be a comprehensive financial, system, and compliance audits of the PUL covering the leadership of the most immediate elected past officers from the 2019 Congress and subsequent elections as well as all transactions undertaken during the course of our crisis, especially from the third week of November 2022 up to the period of the inaugural ceremonies undertaken by the Interim Committee and the Joint Inaugural Committees" ; said that though his administration seeks to reconcile the Union, "let us not forget that reconciliation in the absence of accountability and justice remains elusive if we don't hold people accountable for their stewardship" ; "As we take over the Union today, it is important to know how we are entering and what we are meeting there. This is the beginning of what we stand for when it comes to the first pillar of our agenda, accountability. Findings and recommendations from these reports will be fully implemented where necessary in order to reset and guide the PUL forward."

a4961.speaker: Julius Kanubah, newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.name: Julius Kanubah
a4961.title: newly elected President of the Press Union of Liberia (PUL)
a4961.speech: Announced there will be a comprehensive review of the Union Constitution to include the vexing or emerging question of membership categories, and said: "Aware of the rigid and apparently precedent setting work of the Interim Committee on some of our Full Members who did transition to politics through political appointments or through running or canvassing for national political office or canvassing as party stalwarts or individual political stalwart for politicians, the review will consider the best way forward."

a5086.speaker: Ibrahima Maïga, activist residing in the United States
a5086.name: Ibrahima Maïga
a5086.title: activist residing in the United States
a5086.speech: Made publications accusing UPC president Zéphirin Diabré of taking part, in complicity with Ivorian president Alassane Dramane Ouattara, in a possible destabilisation of the Burkinabè Transition.

a5086.speaker: Zéphirin Diabré, president of the Union for Progress and Change (UPC) (party communiqué on Facebook)
a5086.name: Zéphirin Diabré
a5086.title: president of the Union for Progress and Change (UPC) (party communiqué on Facebook)
a5086.speech: According to a communiqué circulated on the party's Facebook page, has filed a complaint "against Messrs Ibrahima Maiga, Faical Nikiema, Sansan Kambou, Salif Nikiema and several other internet users for defamation, endangering the person of others, and any other offences the investigation may reveal."

a5086.speaker: National Secretariat for Information and Communication (SNIC) of the UPC
a5086.name: National Secretariat for Information and Communication (SNIC) of the UPC
a5086.speech: Made known that a second procedure will be initiated against the perpetrators of these acts abroad, so that they answer for their actions wherever they may be, and a third procedure will be initiated with the company Facebook, the social network where the offences were committed through the publication or sharing of texts, images, videos, comments and other content.

a5087.speaker: Indermit Gill, Vice-President and Chief Economist of the World Bank
a5087.name: Indermit Gill
a5087.title: Vice-President and Chief Economist of the World Bank
a5087.speech: "Interest rates will come down in the future, but they will remain above the pre-COVID-19 pandemic period, which means that the poorest countries will not be able to borrow on terms as advantageous as before." ; Speaking to journalists at the presentation of the International Debt Report released in Washington, said that developing countries spent "a record 1.4 trillion dollars to service their external debt, with the cost of interest rising to its highest level in 20 years" ; noted that the amount paid in interest alone "rose by almost a third to 406 billion dollars, further squeezing budgets in critical areas such as health, education and the environment."

a5087.speaker: Indermit Gill, Vice-President and Chief Economist of the World Bank
a5087.name: Indermit Gill
a5087.title: Vice-President and Chief Economist of the World Bank
a5087.speech: "In the most heavily indebted poor countries, the multilateral development banks are acting as lender of last resort, a role that is not theirs, which reflects a dysfunctional financial system, since with the exception of funds from the World Bank and other multilateral institutions, money is leaving poor economies when it should be coming in."

a5087.speaker: World Bank International Debt Report
a5087.name: World Bank International Debt Report
a5087.speech: "Interest payments rose to their highest level ever, 34.6 billion dollars in 2023, four times more than the amount paid in 2013"; the report notes that the average interest payments for the poorest countries represent 6% of export revenues, a level unseen since 1999, and in some countries this percentage rises to 38%; it concludes that last year external borrowing became "considerably more expensive for all developing economies", as interest rates from official creditors rose to more than 4% and rates charged by private creditors rose by more than a point, to 6%, the highest level in 15 years.

a5267.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (executive order on foreign aid)
a5267.name: Donald Trump
a5267.title: US President (executive order on foreign aid)
a5267.speech: The order instructed all government agencies managing foreign development assistance programmes to halt the disbursement of funds.

a5267.speaker: NPR
a5267.name: NPR
a5267.speech: Reported that PEPFAR has stopped disbursing funding and is likely to suspend operations for at least three months if an exemption is not made for the programme in the coming weeks.

a5267.speaker: US State Department fact sheet
a5267.name: US State Department fact sheet
a5267.speech: Showed that PEPFAR has saved the lives of an estimated 26 million people since its inception.

a5267.speaker: US State Department
a5267.name: US State Department
a5267.speech: Speaking on the ban, the agency was quoted as saying, "The United States is no longer going to blindly dole out money with no return for the American people."

a5267.speaker: Public health experts
a5267.name: Public health experts
a5267.speech: Fear the new Trump administration might terminate the entire programme.

a5324.speaker: CITAC (energy consultancy report)
a5324.name: CITAC (energy consultancy report)
a5324.speech: According to a report from energy consultancy CITAC seen by local media, Nigeria has lost its position as Africa’s largest importer of refined petroleum products, overtaken by South Africa; the report noted that Nigeria’s total refined fuel imports for 2025 are projected to fall to 6.4 million tonnes compared to South Africa’s 15.5 million tonnes.

a5371.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5371.name: Donald Trump
a5371.title: US President
a5371.speech: Announced some radical measures aimed at making America great again when he regained the American presidency a few months ago.

a5371.speaker: Other donors, including the United Kingdom
a5371.name: Other donors
a5371.title: including the United Kingdom
a5371.speech: Have also warned that aid will no longer be a priority.

a5371.speaker: The United States (government announcement)
a5371.name: The United States (government announcement)
a5371.speech: Only last week, the US announced a sudden termination of funding from the Millennium Challenge Corporation.

a5371.speaker: The Trump administration
a5371.name: The Trump administration
a5371.speech: Has made it clear that it views us as careless and irresponsible.

a5371.speaker: US Embassy (statements)
a5371.name: US Embassy (statements)
a5371.speech: Statements made by the US Embassy over the denial of American visas to so-called "Malawian diplomats" — listening to them, one cannot help but feel shame upon realising that our systems are so porous that even our approach to diplomacy cannot be trusted.

a5431.speaker: Dr. Amir Aman, Minister of Health of Ethiopia
a5431.name: Dr. Amir Aman
a5431.title: Minister of Health of Ethiopia
a5431.speech: “Digitizing the system alone doesn’t mean getting solutions end to end rather it is working on the mind set of all stakeholders,” Amir stressed ; “Digitalizing health systems mean a lot for the Ministry as it corrects the data and improves information about the health of our population,” the Minister added.

a5431.speaker: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia
a5431.name: Ministry of Health of Ethiopia
a5431.speech: According to the Ministry of Health, currently 88 percent of health centers are digitized and the rest 22 percent will be incorporated in this fiscal year, adding that the support from USAID is pertinent to the move.

a5431.speaker: Sean Jones, USAID Mission Director
a5431.name: Sean Jones
a5431.title: USAID Mission Director
a5431.speech: “In addition to simply expanding digital health systems and strengthening the skills of today’s medical professionals, we are also increasing our focus on developing the leaders of tomorrow to drive health innovations far into the future.”

a5450.speaker: Abou Hamed Saley, Representative of the international NGO Médecins du Monde (MDM)
a5450.name: Abou Hamed Saley
a5450.title: Representative of the international NGO Médecins du Monde (MDM)
a5450.speech: In handing over the donation to the Governor of the Tahoua Region, recalled that for more than 10 years MDM Belgium in Niger has worked alongside communities to guarantee equitable access to care, notably for the most vulnerable people—women, children, unaccompanied minors and populations on the move ; stressed that this donation aligns with the priorities of the Government of Niger in matters of public health, with a view to contributing to the protection of populations and the reduction of morbidity and mortality ; took the opportunity to thank the authorities of Tahoua and all the actors present who work tirelessly to improve access to health care for target groups, and reaffirmed his institution's commitment to supporting Niger in strengthening its health system through permanent and quality support for the benefit of the population.

a5450.speaker: Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé, Governor of the Tahoua Region
a5450.name: Colonel-Major Oumarou Tawayé
a5450.title: Governor of the Tahoua Region
a5450.speech: In receiving the donation, expressed his deep gratitude to the generous donor; on behalf of the highest Nigerien authorities, conveyed his encouragement and congratulations to the NGO Médecins du Monde for this support, so important for health facilities, which comes at a time when the CNSP military authorities have lowered the fees for patient care services and in a context of refoundation ; gave assurances that this donation will go directly to the beneficiaries.

a5475.speaker: European Union
a5475.name: European Union
a5475.speech: Announced an initial humanitarian aid package of 1.9 billion euros for 2025, of which 510 million euros is intended for Nigeria and other sub-Saharan African countries.

a5475.speaker: European Commission (communiqué)
a5475.name: European Commission (communiqué)
a5475.speech: Said on Thursday that "these funds should be channelled to West and Central Africa, the Sahel, the Lake Chad basin, north-western Nigeria, Central Africa, the Great Lakes region and the Greater Horn of Africa." The statement adds that the Middle East and North Africa will receive 470 million euros, of which 375 million euros is concentrated on the Middle East, particularly Gaza, while 95 million euros is allocated to North Africa and Yemen.

a5475.speaker: European Union
a5475.name: European Union
a5475.speech: Noted that the aid would help address the escalating humanitarian crises expected to affect more than 300 million people worldwide in 2025.

a5475.speaker: Hadja Lahbib, European Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness and Crisis Management
a5475.name: Hadja Lahbib
a5475.title: European Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness and Crisis Management
a5475.speech: Stressed the importance of guaranteeing safe and unimpeded access to vulnerable populations and that funding alone is insufficient without respect for international humanitarian law ; "Our humanitarian aid funding will support our partners on the ground - the United Nations family, the Red Cross and Red Crescent family, international and local governments and non-governmental organisations - to deliver life-saving emergency assistance where it is needed."

a5587.speaker: Gladson Kaunda, 15, Chairperson of the Wash club at Mbande Primary School
a5587.name: Gladson Kaunda
a5587.title: 15, Chairperson of the Wash club at Mbande Primary School
a5587.speech: “We meet every Monday. Since the club was founded, our school and homes have become cleaner and healthier. We were provided with buckets, soap and sanitary pads to promote good hygiene practices” ; said the new habits — regular hand washing with soap, cleaning their surroundings, responsibly disposing of waste and drinking water from treated sources — have become routine for the students.

a5587.speaker: Gladson Kaunda, 15, Chairperson of the Wash club at Mbande Primary School
a5587.name: Gladson Kaunda
a5587.title: 15, Chairperson of the Wash club at Mbande Primary School
a5587.speech: “Through our efforts, we persuaded the school committee to construct more toilets and provide sanitary spaces for adolescent girls.”

a5587.speaker: Chimwemwe Mhango, Headteacher of Mbande Primary School
a5587.name: Chimwemwe Mhango
a5587.title: Headteacher of Mbande Primary School
a5587.speech: Notes that the proactive behaviour of the Wash club has had a ripple effect, making the school a model for neighbouring institutions ; “Previously, absenteeism due to waterborne diseases was a major issue. But now, that is all in the past. For the first time, the school has recorded its highest pass rate in the recently released primary school leaving examinations” ; attributes this success partly to the students’ improved health and understanding of disease prevention.

a5587.speaker: Chimwemwe Mhango, Headteacher of Mbande Primary School
a5587.name: Chimwemwe Mhango
a5587.title: Headteacher of Mbande Primary School
a5587.speech: “Information is power and prevention is better than cure. We are committed to maintaining this momentum for long-term change” ; “Together, we are building a healthier future”, expressing optimism for the continued success of the Wash initiatives at her school and beyond.

a5587.speaker: Mbasakile Mwafulirwa, Chairperson of the Mwankenja Village health committee
a5587.name: Mbasakile Mwafulirwa
a5587.title: Chairperson of the Mwankenja Village health committee
a5587.speech: Explains that the door-to-door water chlorination initiative began in November 2023 and continues to be carried out twice a month ; “We visit 65 households in our area, and I am pleased to report that we have not had a single cholera case in the past year.”

a5822.speaker: SAFI TIMBER, Import & Export (company position)
a5822.name: SAFI TIMBER
a5822.title: Import & Export (company position)
a5822.speech: Considers illegal the decision suspending its timber export licence issued by the Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries (MAAP); holds that there was a violation of administrative principles, corruption and an attempt at extortion, and accuses senior MAAP officials of being behind a campaign aimed at extorting 15 million meticais from SAFI TIMBER; appeals for the intervention of the Central Office for Combating Corruption (GCCC).

a5822.speaker: Mozambican Federation of Timber Operators (FEDEMOMA) (communique)
a5822.name: Mozambican Federation of Timber Operators (FEDEMOMA) (communique)
a5822.speech: According to a FEDEMOMA communique, the Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries, Roberto Albino, suspended with immediate effect the native timber export licence of SAFI TIMBER, Import & Export — Export Certificate number 01/MTA/2025.

a5822.speaker: SAFI TIMBER, Import & Export (note sent to the newsroom)
a5822.name: SAFI TIMBER
a5822.title: Import & Export (note sent to the newsroom)
a5822.speech: Explains that, having consulted the Administrative Procedure Code, it found that, first, "the maximum deadline for notification of administrative acts is five days"; second, "administrative acts must be notified directly to the interested party"; "a prior hearing is mandatory whenever the decision negatively affects the rights of a party", as well as "decisions must be reasoned, indicating the grounds and the legal basis" ; holds that the seven-day delay in notification and the absence of a prior hearing constitute a clear violation of the principles of legality, transparency and good administration provided for in law.

a5822.speaker: SAFI TIMBER, Import & Export (aggrieved company)
a5822.name: SAFI TIMBER
a5822.title: Import & Export (aggrieved company)
a5822.speech: Says that on 12 August its representatives received several telephone calls from different numbers and were pressured to make an illicit payment of 15 million meticais, under threat of definitive cancellation of the export certificate; accuses Imede Falume, national director of Forests and Wildlife, and Renato Timane, adviser to the Minister of Agriculture, Environment and Fisheries, of being involved in the attempt.

a5822.speaker: SAFI TIMBER, Import & Export (company position)
a5822.name: SAFI TIMBER
a5822.title: Import & Export (company position)
a5822.speech: Says it refuses to be complicit with corruption and will trigger legal mechanisms so that the two accused are held judicially responsible for corruption and extortion; considers that the suspension of its export certificate is not only illegal but also a clear attempt at extortion that is causing enormous financial losses and staining the credibility of the forestry sector in Mozambique; requests the intervention of the Attorney General’s Office and of the Central Office for Combating Corruption for an investigation and accountability of the transgressors.

a5930.speaker: Northern Elders Forum (NEF) communiqué
a5930.name: Northern Elders Forum (NEF) communiqué
a5930.speech: Called on President Bola Tinubu to declare a state of emergency in northern Nigeria, citing the extraordinary scale of insecurity and the government’s constitutional and international obligations to protect lives; lamented that state security agencies remained overstretched, under-resourced, and in some cases complicit through inaction, leaving citizens vulnerable while eroding public trust in government; expressed grave concern over the spate of violent attacks, abductions and killings across the region, warning that continued inaction could threaten Nigeria’s stability and regional peace; recalled the August 19 attack on a mosque in Unguwan Mantau village, where armed assailants killed at least 27 worshippers during early morning prayers; condemned the execution of 35 abductees in Zamfara State despite ransom payments, as well as two separate attacks in Kaduna State’s Kauru and Kudan LGAs, which left eight dead and eight others severely injured.

a5930.speaker: Professor Abubakar Jika Jiddere, spokesperson of the Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a5930.name: Professor Abubakar Jika Jiddere
a5930.title: spokesperson of the Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a5930.speech: “These incidents are not isolated cases, rather they are part of a persistent pattern of organised criminal violence and banditry that have claimed thousands of lives, displaced hundreds of thousands of citizens, undermined food security, crippled economic activity, and inflicted deep psychological and social trauma on individuals and several communities. The NEF observes with deep regret that the state security architecture remains inadequate, overstretched, and in some cases complicit through inaction and silence, leaving citizens vulnerable and helpless while eroding public trust in government institutions.”

a5930.speaker: Professor Abubakar Jika Jiddere, spokesperson of the Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a5930.name: Professor Abubakar Jika Jiddere
a5930.title: spokesperson of the Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a5930.speech: Citing the 1999 constitution, the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, and the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, said: “Article 6 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR), states that, the inherent right to life shall be protected by law, and no one shall arbitrarily be deprived of life. The recurring atrocities in Northern Nigeria constitute serious breaches of these obligations, and in their scale and persistence, will amount to crimes against humanity under international law and humanitarian cases.”

a5930.speaker: Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a5930.name: Northern Elders Forum (NEF)
a5930.speech: Urged the Federal Government to “declare a state of emergency in Northern Nigeria, acknowledging the extraordinary scale of the crisis. Deploy adequately trained, armed, and equipped security forces with clear rules of engagement to protect civilian populations and secure international border regions. Provide adequate compensation, rehabilitation, and humanitarian assistance to victims including displaced persons, in line with international humanitarian standards. Strengthen border control and regional cooperation with neighbouring states under ECOWAS and the African Union protocols, to stem cross-border incursions by armed criminal groups. Engage international partners, including the African Union (AU) and United Nations (UN), for technical and humanitarian support” ; further warned that the continued inaction or insufficient responses to all these security challenges will not only exacerbate human suffering, but also jeopardise national cohesion, democratic sustainability, stability of the polity, and regional peace; called on the government to act immediately, decisively, transparently and in full alignment with Nigeria’s domestic and international obligations; pledged to continue monitoring developments while engaging stakeholders nationally and internationally to ensure urgent relief for affected Northern communities.

a6107.speaker: Yoweri Museveni, President of Uganda
a6107.name: Yoweri Museveni
a6107.title: President of Uganda
a6107.speech: Has often highlighted the potential for BRICS partnerships to attract foreign investment in Uganda's agricultural produce like coffee and tea.

a6164.speaker: Ministry of Education (Malawi)
a6164.name: Ministry of Education (Malawi)
a6164.speech: Has called for the streamlining of roles and processes to minimise cases of double accreditation which is a duplication of efforts.

a6164.speaker: Levis Eneya, Director of Higher Education, Ministry of Education
a6164.name: Levis Eneya
a6164.title: Director of Higher Education, Ministry of Education
a6164.speech: Said this in Lilongwe at the opening of a stakeholder meeting of regulatory bodies held to discuss the ongoing development of the Higher Education Bill; acknowledged the critical role of regulatory bodies in maintaining quality higher education standards, emphasising the need to enhance the regulation of higher education and address concerns such as the duplication of accreditation: “The Bill offers an opportunity to clearly define responsibilities, reducing confusion among higher education institutions and ensuring alignment with the mandates of professional bodies.”

a6164.speaker: Ambumulire Phiri, Chief Executive Officer, National Council for Higher Education (Nche)
a6164.name: Ambumulire Phiri
a6164.title: Chief Executive Officer, National Council for Higher Education (Nche)
a6164.speech: Highlighted the importance of collaboration and stakeholder contributions to the Bill and reaffirmed Nche’s commitment to ensuring the Bill addresses stakeholder concerns while improving service delivery in the higher education sector: “Nche has successfully collaborated with professional bodies in various programmes, such as in the joint assessments for legal education programmes. There is a need for explicit guidelines in the Bill to delineate responsibilities for regulating different academic programmes, which will ensure efficiency and clarity.”

a6164.speaker: Mary Chitsulo, USAid representative
a6164.name: Mary Chitsulo
a6164.title: USAid representative
a6164.speech: Hailed the collaborative approach, highlighting the importance of understanding operational dynamics to streamline registration and accreditation processes in the country’s higher education sub-sector.

a6185.speaker: Ben M'bwana, Director of Administration at the Ministry of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare
a6185.name: Ben M'bwana
a6185.title: Director of Administration at the Ministry of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare
a6185.speech: Hailed the challenge, saying bicycles can have a positive impact when it comes to economic empowerment, improved health outcomes and education access in Malawi: "Bicycles are not just a means of transport; they are a transformative tool for development and empowerment. In Sub-Saharan Africa, where over 78% of the population relies on walking to access work and essential services, bicycles can significantly enhance mobility and economic opportunities."

a6217.speaker: Getachew Reda, President of the Tigray Region Interim Administration
a6217.name: Getachew Reda
a6217.title: President of the Tigray Region Interim Administration
a6217.speech: In a statement on Dimtsi Weyane Television on Sunday evening, held himself too accountable for the Tigray crisis and said every party bears responsibility for the crisis in the Tigray region ; Said that when he demands the return of Western Tigray, federal government people answer him: “Forget Humera; first administer Axum properly”, and stated that the TPLF head office group has been an obstacle preventing his administration from having a strong foundation and from properly protecting Tigray’s interests.

a6217.speaker: Getachew Reda, President of the Tigray Region Interim Administration
a6217.name: Getachew Reda
a6217.title: President of the Tigray Region Interim Administration
a6217.speech: “The federal government tramples on us as it pleases because of our own weakness. The federal government lacks good faith in implementing the agreement. The main party responsible, bearing about 70 percent of the responsibility for the problem, is the weakness within ourselves. Many problems were created because our negotiating capacity has weakened. When we ourselves waste the opportunity and create problems for ourselves, how can we expect others to worry about us more than we do? We have been told: do not ask us for Humera when you cannot administer Axum. When we say Western Tigray should be returned, they told us that we ourselves are the obstacle to the return of the displaced. As long as we go to Addis Ababa and raise a question of power rather than the issue of the displaced, no different answer can be expected. There is no force in Tigray that, in collaboration with external or internal forces, is attacking the federal government.”

a6217.speaker: Getachew Reda, President of the Tigray Region Interim Administration
a6217.name: Getachew Reda
a6217.title: President of the Tigray Region Interim Administration
a6217.speech: Made a calming appeal, saying that the security force should not be thrown into turmoil because of the political leadership’s problems.

a6217.speaker: TPLF Central Control (Auditing) Commission (statement of Tir 14, 2017 E.C.)
a6217.name: TPLF Central Control (Auditing) Commission (statement of Tir 14
a6217.title: 2017 E.C.)
a6217.speech: Blamed the interim administration for Tigray’s problems.

a6217.speaker: Leaders of the Tigray army (statement)
a6217.name: Leaders of the Tigray army (statement)
a6217.speech: Criticised the interim administration, went as far as urging that a change be made to it, publicly announced that they give full support to the group led by Debretsion (Dr) which runs the TPLF head office, accused the interim administration of colluding with the enemy, and demanded that the administration be changed ; Ordered that no marches or protests be held in the region.

a6217.speaker: Salsay Weyane Tigray (opposition party, statement)
a6217.name: Salsay Weyane Tigray (opposition party
a6217.title: statement)
a6217.speech: Condemned the political interference of the military leaders and described the order that “no protest demonstrations be held” as a Derg-style command.

a6217.speaker: Coalition of parties including Arena Tigray and Baytona (joint statement)
a6217.name: Coalition of parties including Arena Tigray and Baytona (joint statement)
a6217.speech: Strongly condemned the political interference of the military leaders.

a6217.speaker: Gebru Asrat, veteran Arena party politician and former TPLF fighter
a6217.name: Gebru Asrat
a6217.title: veteran Arena party politician and former TPLF fighter
a6217.speech: Described the recent situation as the occasion on which the Tigray army leaders openly declared their alliance with the TPLF group of Debretsion (Dr), and said he found the military officers’ decision to be one with “no legal, institutional or constitutional basis.”

a6217.speaker: Gebru Asrat, veteran Arena party politician and former TPLF fighter
a6217.name: Gebru Asrat
a6217.title: veteran Arena party politician and former TPLF fighter
a6217.speech: “The TPLF group of Debretsion (Dr) is working to oppose and delegitimise the senior army commanders by gathering so-called corps commanders and mid-level commanders who were former TPLF cadres. It is not the top leaders but those below who declared that they stand with the TPLF. The youth, however, understood this and came out to protest. Large peaceful demonstrations have been held in Tigray’s towns, including Mekelle. The youth opposed them, saying ‘you are Shaebia’s errand boys.’ What the youth are saying is that even the TPLF’s political cadres and leadership are no longer needed for Tigray at this time, and in such a situation they are publicly expressing their anger that the military leaders have abandoned their neutrality, intervened in politics and are striving to bring the TPLF back from the dead.”

a6217.speaker: Gebru Asrat, veteran Arena party politician and former TPLF fighter
a6217.name: Gebru Asrat
a6217.title: veteran Arena party politician and former TPLF fighter
a6217.speech: “About 200 army leaders gathered. Of these, however, some 25 — senior officers at that — opposed the matter and walked out... Among the 25 officers who walked out are key commanders such as Wedi Ashebir, Wedi Abate and Wedi Antiru. Twelve of them are generals said to hold decisive leadership authority... The officers’ decision that the army must side with the TPLF head office group and stand against the interim administration has itself divided the army’s commanders.
